cases.people: Da Afghanistan Bank supervisors (unnamed)
cases.summary: A May 2011 report by Afghanistan's High Office of Oversight and Anticorruption singled out the central bank for poor monitoring of Kabul Bank, which had $925 million in outstanding loans, many undocumented and given to powerful figures, before the central bank took it over in 2010.
cases.source_title: Afghan Anticorruption Commission Attacks Regulators In Bank Scandal (RFE/RL)

cases.people: Valter Filipe da Silva (governor); António Samalia Bule Manuel (senior BNA manager); José Filomeno dos Santos (head of sovereign fund); Jorge Gaudens Pontes Sebastião (businessman)
cases.summary: On 14 August 2020 Angola's Supreme Court convicted former governor Valter Filipe (eight years), BNA manager Samalia (five years), José Filomeno dos Santos (five years) and businessman Sebastião (six years) of embezzlement, fraud and influence peddling over an attempted illicit transfer of $500 million to a London account, which a British bank blocked. After the Constitutional Court annulled the ruling, the Supreme Court plenary confirmed the convictions in 2024.
cases.source_title: Tribunal Supremo confirma condenações no caso '500 milhões' (Ver Angola / Lusa)

cases.people: Ardian Fullani (governor); Elivar Golemi (senior auditor)
cases.summary: On 5 September 2014 prosecutors arrested governor Fullani and the bank's senior auditor, charging them with abuse of office for alleged mismanagement linked to the theft of Lek 713 million (nearly $7 million) from the Bank of Albania's reserves by a central bank employee, discovered in July 2014; the board dismissed Fullani.
cases.source_title: Officials look to shore up central bank following governor's arrest (Tirana Times)

cases.central_bank: Banco Central de la República Argentina
cases.people: Alejandro Vanoli (former BCRA president); Miguel Ángel Pesce (BCRA president at the time of the 2021 ruling); Cristina Fernández de Kirchner; Axel Kicillof
cases.summary: Vanoli, Pesce, former president Fernández de Kirchner, former economy minister Kicillof and others were tried for defrauding the state through BCRA sales of dollar futures between August and November 2015. On 13 April 2021 the Federal Court of Criminal Cassation unanimously dismissed the case against all 15 defendants.
cases.source_title: Dólar futuro: sobreseyeron a Cristina, a Axel Kicillof y al resto de los acusados (La Capital)

cases.central_bank: Banco Central de la República Argentina
cases.people: Miguel Ángel Pesce (BCRA president); Sergio Massa (economy minister)
cases.summary: In May 2023, an election year, the BCRA transferred another ARS 140 billion to the Treasury through temporary advances (adelantos transitorios), bringing transfers since March to ARS 370 billion and using 99.2% of the ARS 372.8 billion first-half limit agreed with the IMF.
cases.source_title: Más emisión: el BCRA volvió a financiar al Tesoro y agota el límite del FMI (Bloomberg Línea)

cases.people: Securency and Note Printing Australia (RBA subsidiaries); John Ellery (Securency CFO); Radius Christanto (agent in Indonesia)
cases.summary: In October 2011 RBA subsidiaries Securency and NPA pleaded guilty to conspiring to bribe foreign officials to win banknote business with note-issuing authorities of Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Nepal; they paid proceeds-of-crime penalties of A$19.8 million and A$1.86 million and fines of A$480,000 and A$450,000. Securency's former CFO received a suspended six-month sentence for false accounting (2012) and agent Radius Christanto a suspended two-year sentence (2013).
cases.source_title: Chronology: Events related to charges against Note Printing Australia and Securency (Reserve Bank of Australia)

cases.people: Wolfgang Duchatczek (OeNB deputy governor and OeBS board chairman); Michael Wolf and Johannes Miller (OeBS CEOs); Kurt Meyer (Austrian Mint CEO); sales staff and two lawyers
cases.summary: Former managers of OeBS, the OeNB's banknote printing subsidiary, were tried for paying kickbacks to the central banks of Azerbaijan (20% overcharge) and Syria (14%) to win banknote orders, with about €14 million paid. Seven defendants were convicted in October 2014; after a Supreme Court-ordered retrial, the Vienna court in February 2018 gave Wolf and Miller 18-month suspended terms and Meyer 21 months suspended, while former OeNB deputy governor Duchatczek was acquitted.
cases.source_title: More lenient sentence in the second instance in OeBS bribery scandal (CoinsWeekly)

cases.people: Firangiz Hajiyeva, Konul Ismayilova, Ershad Jalilov, Shahnaz Samadova, Nazila Bagirova, Sabina Mammadova (former central bank officers)
cases.summary: In September 2009 a Baku court sentenced six former central bank officers to terms from a two-year suspended sentence to eight years for abuse of power and embezzlement of AZN 1.4 million from the Central Bank between 2003 and 2008.
cases.source_title: Court passes judgment on former officers of Azerbaijan's Central Bank (APA)

cases.people: Unnamed decision makers at the Central Bank of Azerbaijan
cases.summary: A Vienna court found that Austrian banknote printer OeBS overcharged the Central Bank of Azerbaijan by 20% on banknote contracts and that the kickback returned to local decision makers; OeBS managers were convicted in 2014 and on retrial in 2018. No Azerbaijani official was named or tried in these proceedings.
cases.source_title: Verdicts in the OeBS kickback affair (CoinsWeekly)

cases.people: Sitangshu Kumar Sur Chowdhury (SK Sur, deputy governor until January 2018)
cases.summary: On 14 January 2025 Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Commission arrested former deputy governor SK Sur in a case filed for failing to submit an asset statement; the ACC had opened an investigation in 2022 into allegations that while at the central bank he facilitated and benefited from the loan scam run by PK Halder.
cases.source_title: Former BB deputy governor SK Sur arrested (Prothom Alo)

cases.people: Atiur Rahman (former governor); records also sought on governors Fazle Kabir and Abdur Rouf Talukder and several deputy governors and BFIU heads
cases.summary: In June 2025 the Anti-Corruption Commission opened an investigation into former governor Atiur Rahman over alleged abuse of power, policies favouring loan defaulters and enabling frauds such as the Hallmark and S Alam Group scandals, and the 2016 reserve heist; it sought central bank records on two other former governors and several deputy governors. The ACC had prosecuted Atiur in February 2025 over the AnonTex loan scam.
cases.source_title: ACC begins investigating ex-BB governor Atiur (The Financial Express)

cases.people: Unnamed Bangladesh Bank officials; inquiry led by former governor Mohammed Farashuddin
cases.summary: Attackers used Bangladesh Bank's SWIFT access on the night of 4 February 2016 to steal reserves from its New York Fed account ($101 million per The Daily Star; $81 million extracted per Prothom Alo). The government inquiry committee's final report of 30 May 2016 hinted at involvement of central bank officials and, according to Prothom Alo, named employees for action; the report was never published and no one was punished as of 2019.
cases.source_title: Govt probe hints at BB officials' links (The Daily Star)

cases.people: Tsvetan Gounev (deputy governor for banking supervision 2013-2015); Rumen Simeonov (former deputy governor for banking supervision)
cases.summary: Bulgarian prosecutors charged two former BNB deputy governors in charge of supervision with failing to take legally required measures against Corporate Commercial Bank (Corpbank) from February 2010, allegedly to benefit its shareholders; Gounev was charged in June 2014 and removed from office by court order in December 2014, and Simeonov was charged about ten months later. Corpbank collapsed in June 2014; its majority owner was accused of embezzling 206 million leva.
cases.source_title: Former Central Bank Chief Supervisor Charged with Inaction in Respect of Corpbank (BTA)

cases.people: A former central bank president and three other former senior officials, including former director Edwin Rojas
cases.summary: On 28 April 2026 Bolivian authorities detained the former central bank president and three other former senior officials over seven debt-swap operations with local financial entities in June-July 2024 at inflated prices, which cost the state $142.3 million; the vice minister of transparency said price records were later altered on internal email instructions to hide the overvaluation. The suspects deny wrongdoing; seven people are under investigation.
cases.source_title: Bolivia arresta a exdirectivos del banco central por canjes de bonos inflados (Bloomberg Línea)

cases.people: Unnamed banker (BTG Pactual fund) and senior federal government officials of the time
cases.summary: On 3 October 2019 Brazil's Federal Police and the São Paulo federal prosecutors launched Operation Estrela Cadente into leaks of Copom interest-rate decisions in 2010, 2011 and 2012 to benefit a BTG Pactual fund, investigating passive and active corruption, insider information and money laundering. Details remained under court seal.
cases.source_title: MPF e PF deflagram operação sobre vazamentos do Copom em favor de fundo do BTG (Jovem Pan / Estadão Conteúdo)

cases.people: Philipp Hildebrand (chairman of the governing board); Kashya Hildebrand (wife)
cases.summary: Hildebrand resigned on 9 January 2012 after reports that dollar trades made in 2011 from a joint account with his wife earned tens of thousands of dollars while the SNB was acting to weaken the franc. He said the trades broke no rules but that he could not prove he was unaware of them; he donated the profits to charity.
cases.source_title: Central banker quits over private currency deal (swissinfo.ch)

cases.people: Fan Yifei (deputy governor of the PBOC)
cases.summary: In October 2024 the Huanggang Intermediate People's Court sentenced former PBOC deputy governor Fan Yifei to death with a two-year reprieve, to be commuted to life without parole, for accepting property worth more than 386 million yuan by taking advantage of his posts at the central bank and other institutions including China Construction Bank.
cases.source_title: Former China deputy central bank head gets suspended death sentence for taking bribes (VOA via Citizen Digital)

cases.country: Cameroon (BEAC, regional central bank of CEMAC)
cases.central_bank: Banque des États de l'Afrique Centrale
cases.people: Roger Kemadjou (head of BEAC's Paris office and governor's delegate 1998-2008); Jean Félix Mamalépot (governor, 1992-2007); Philibert Andzembé (governor)
cases.summary: A November 2009 internal BEAC report found about 20 billion CFA francs were diverted from the bank's Paris office to 139 beneficiaries between 2004 and 2008. On 28 September 2012 a court in Mfoundi, Cameroon, sentenced Kemadjou to life imprisonment and ordered him to pay BEAC 26.4 billion CFA francs. The BEAC's internal report on the Paris office fraud, published in late October 2009, put the loss at about 25 million euros and described internal controls as far below international standards. It said alarming reports were sent to the governor but no firm action followed, and the article blames governor Mamalépot for not acting and criticizes governor Andzembé for letting the scheme continue. Jean-Pierre Oyiba, chief of staff to Gabon's president, resigned on 9 November 2009 after the report said he received about 100,000 euros, which he denies.
cases.source_title: BEAC : Les auteurs du détournement du BEP condamnés (Gabonreview)
cases.update_title: Le scandale de la BEAC révèle carences, dérives et laxisme (Webmanagercenter)

cases.central_bank: Centrale Bank van Curaçao en Sint Maarten
cases.people: Emsley Tromp (president-director); Rene Laurents (deputy director)
cases.summary: In July 2024 a court found former central bank president Tromp and former deputy director Laurents guilty of document forgery over a backdated 2009 loan agreement under which over $400,000 went to Tromp's pension account, and acquitted them of official bribery and money laundering, including over a $1.5 million 2015 payment from Venezuelan company Enpiso linked by prosecutors to Girobank takeover talks.
cases.source_title: Former Central Bank President Emsley Tromp convicted (Curaçao Chronicle)

cases.people: Ernst Welteke (president 1999-2004)
cases.summary: Welteke resigned on 16 April 2004 after criticism for accepting a free New Year stay at Berlin's Hotel Adlon paid by a commercial bank two years earlier; the Bundesbank oversees commercial banks, and prosecutors and the Bundesbank had opened inquiries.
cases.source_title: German central bank chief quits (AP via NBC News)

cases.people: Benoît Cœuré (Executive Board member)
cases.summary: On 18 May 2015 Cœuré told a private evening event in London that the ECB would front-load asset purchases; the speech was published only the next morning, which the ECB attributed to an 'internal procedure error'. Draghi said no market-sensitive information was revealed.
cases.source_title: Draghi defends ECB participation in private events (Central Banking)

cases.people: Mario Draghi (ECB President)
cases.summary: In case 1697/2016/ANA the European Ombudsman found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that Draghi suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, saying membership was not in keeping with the ECB's independence. The ECB declined, and Draghi did not suspend his membership.
cases.source_title: European Ombudsman press release on ECB President's G30 membership (18 April 2018)

cases.people: Bank of England staff and auction participants (unnamed)
cases.summary: The Bank self-referred material about its 2007-2008 liquidity auctions to the Serious Fraud Office, which opened an investigation in 2015 and closed it in June 2017, concluding there was no evidence of criminality.
cases.source_title: Statement on SFO liquidity auction investigation announcement (Bank of England)

cases.people: Charlotte Hogg (deputy governor for markets and banking; previously chief operating officer)
cases.summary: Hogg resigned on 14 March 2017 after the House of Commons Treasury Committee published a report finding that her failure, on multiple occasions since joining the Bank in 2013, to declare her brother's role as director of group strategy at Barclays was a 'very serious breach'; she said she had also unintentionally misled the committee.
cases.source_title: Tyrie welcomes Bank of England deputy's resignation after 'serious breach' (Mortgage Solutions)

cases.people: Johnson Pandit Asiama (second deputy governor); Kwabena Duffuor (former BoG governor, uniBank shareholder)
cases.summary: In February 2020 Ghana's Attorney-General charged former finance minister and ex-BoG governor Duffuor and seven others with 68 counts over the collapse of uniBank; former BoG second deputy governor Asiama was accused of using his position to approve the transfer of a GH¢300 million unsecured credit facility from distressed uniBank to Universal Merchant Bank. Duffuor was charged with dishonestly receiving GH¢663.28 million and money laundering.
cases.source_title: Duffuor, Asiama, Amoabeng, others hauled before court (Graphic Online)

cases.people: Bank of Ghana leadership (not named in source)
cases.summary: In a February 2023 statement the Bank of Ghana said its claims on government at December 2022 included a GH¢37.9 billion overdraft to the government to cover auction shortfalls and pay maturing bonds, GH¢7.2 billion of treasury bonds bought from banks and GH¢8.9 billion of on-lent IMF funds; the government, BoG and IMF had earlier adopted zero deficit financing.
cases.source_title: BoG justifies financing of government's 2022 budget (Ghanaian Times)

cases.central_bank: Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée
cases.people: Ibrahima Chérif Bah (governor 2005-2010)
cases.summary: On 23 June 2026 the appeals chamber of Guinea's CRIEF court convicted former governor Bah in absentia of embezzlement of public funds and related offences, sentencing him to five years and ordering repayment of $10.5 million taken from the central bank's coffers without trace, a GNF 5 billion fine and confiscation of assets; his defence said the funds were released on instruction of the highest state authorities for an international humanitarian organisation.
cases.source_title: Guinée: L'ancien gouverneur de la Banque centrale condamné en appel pour détournement de fonds (RFI via allAfrica)

cases.people: Yannis Stournaras (governor; former finance minister)
cases.summary: On 29 August 2019 Greek prosecutors dropped charges that governor Stournaras accepted bribes from Novartis while finance minister, along with charges against six other former senior officials; the allegations concerned 2001 onward and predated his central bank post.
cases.source_title: Greek authorities drop corruption probe into governor (Central Banking)

cases.people: 11 current and former BCH staff including Arlen Fernando Cerrato Díaz (San Pedro Sula branch manager) and Virgilio Antonio Villalobo Gálvez (former division head)
cases.summary: On 3 June 2026 Honduran prosecutors charged 11 current and former Banco Central de Honduras employees, two of them serving managers, with 100 counts of negligent embezzlement over a scheme that allegedly removed public funds from the central bank over several years; they were arrested after the court admitted the case.
cases.source_title: Capturan a 11 funcionarios y exfuncionarios del BCH por presunto desfalco (El Heraldo)

cases.people: Boris Vujčić (governor); Sandra Švaljek (deputy governor) and other employees
cases.summary: In January 2022 the Zagreb prosecution and market regulator HANFA opened probes into whether senior central bank officials traded securities of supervised commercial banks using insider information, after media reports. The HNB said its executives sold bank shares before the ban took effect and that bond trading was not prohibited.
cases.source_title: Croatia probes alleged insider trading by central bank management (bne IntelliNews)

cases.people: Pallas Athéné foundations established by the Magyar Nemzeti Bank
cases.summary: After the Constitutional Court ruled on 31 March 2016 that the MNB's Pallas Athéné foundations were managing public funds subject to scrutiny, the Public Procurement Board found in June 2016 that public procurement law applied to the six foundations and fined each 200,000 forints, a minor fine because they had requested the review. The MNB had endowed the foundations, set up in 2014, with a little over 267 billion forints.
cases.source_title: NBH Scandal – Central Bank Foundations Fined For Dodging Public Procurement Rules (MTI via XpatLoop)

cases.people: György Matolcsy (governor 2013-2025); Ádám Matolcsy (son); Pallas Athéné Domus Meriti Foundation and asset manager Optima
cases.summary: In March 2025 the State Audit Office (ASZ) published a 373-page report on the MNB-controlled foundations, finding mismanagement of public funds, lack of oversight and losses of hundreds of billions of forints, and filed a criminal complaint over multiple suspected offences. The report focused on the Pallas Athéné Domus Meriti Foundation and its asset manager Optima.
cases.source_title: Hungary's State Audit Office files criminal complaint over operation of National Bank foundations (bne IntelliNews)

cases.people: György Matolcsy (former governor)
cases.summary: On 21 October 2026 former governor Matolcsy was detained and taken to the Central Chief Prosecution Office of Investigation on suspicion of economic fraud causing significant financial damage and use of a forged private document, according to his lawyer; other people, including a lawyer and a businessman, were also detained.
cases.source_title: Former Hungarian central bank governor Matolcsy detained (Daily News Hungary)

cases.people: Unnamed officials of the note-issuing authority; bribe payers: Securency and NPA
cases.summary: In October 2011 Securency and NPA (subsidiaries of the Reserve Bank of Australia) pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials to obtain banknote business with the note-issuing authority of Indonesia between 1999-2001. The officials are not named in the RBA chronology.
cases.source_title: Chronology: Events related to charges against Note Printing Australia and Securency (Reserve Bank of Australia)

cases.people: Burhanuddin Abdullah (governor 2003-2008); Aulia Pohan, Maman Sumantri, Bun Bunan Hutapea, Aslim Tadjuddin (former deputy governors)
cases.summary: In October 2008 the Corruption Court sentenced former governor Burhanuddin Abdullah to five years (raised to five and a half years by the Jakarta High Court in February 2009) for approving the use of Rp 100 billion of BI funds in 2003 to pay legal fees for officials in a liquidity-support graft case and to bribe legislators over an amendment to the BI law. The KPK arrested four former deputy governors, including Aulia Pohan, in November 2008.
cases.source_title: Court extends prison term for ex-BI chief (The Jakarta Post)

cases.people: Budi Mulya (deputy governor)
cases.summary: In July 2014 the anti-corruption court sentenced Budi Mulya to 10 years and a Rp500 million fine for corruption in granting a Rp689.39 billion short-term loan facility to Bank Century and declaring it a failed bank with systemic impact in 2008; the court found he acted partly to save Rp83 billion deposited by a BI employees' foundation and received a Rp1 billion loan from owner Robert Tantular. The court put state losses at Rp8.5 trillion including the Rp6.7 trillion bailout.
cases.source_title: Budi Mulya Sentenced to 10 Years' Imprisonment (Antara)

cases.people: Heri Gunawan and Satori (members of parliament, formerly on Commission XI overseeing BI)
cases.summary: In August 2025 the KPK named two House members as suspects in the alleged misuse of corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds from Bank Indonesia and the Financial Services Authority (OJK), channelled after closed-door budget discussions in 2020-2022 by the commission that approves BI's budget.
cases.source_title: Two lawmakers named graft suspects in BI and OJK CSR scandal (Indonesia Business Post)

cases.people: K. Michael (RBI official, Bangalore)
cases.summary: In December 2016, during demonetisation, India's Central Bureau of Investigation arrested RBI official K. Michael in Bangalore for allegedly converting 15 million rupees (about $222,000) of withdrawn 500 and 1,000 rupee notes into 100 rupee notes without legal documentation, working with a state bank employee.
cases.source_title: India arrests central bank official over cash scam (AFP via The Peninsula)

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of the Islamic Republic of Iran
cases.people: Valiollah Seif (governor 2013-2018); Ahmad Araghchi (deputy governor for foreign currency affairs); Salar Aghakhani
cases.summary: In October 2021 a Tehran court sentenced former governor Seif to 10 years in prison for 'participation in disrupting the country's financial system through illegal smuggling of foreign currency', former deputy Araghchi to eight years, and intermediary Salar Aghakhani to 13 years, over an illegal foreign-currency distribution scheme in 2017-2018. The judiciary said 10 people were identified in the scheme. According to Iran Times, the Supreme Court overturned the verdicts in 2023 citing insufficient evidence and authorisation by higher authorities, and the judiciary dropped the prosecution of Seif and Araghchi in March 2025.
cases.source_title: Iran's ex-central bank chief and officials sentenced to prison (Al Jazeera)

cases.people: Sinan al-Shabibi (governor 2003-2012) and other bank officials
cases.summary: In October 2012 Iraq's cabinet removed governor al-Shabibi after a parliamentary committee charged that bank officials were abusing the central bank's dollar sales, and the Supreme Judicial Council confirmed arrest warrants for him and other officials without giving the charges. His defence called the case politically motivated.
cases.source_title: Iraq issues arrest warrant for ex cenbank chief, other officials (Reuters via The Peninsula)

cases.people: Central Bank of Iraq dollar auction (no individuals named)
cases.summary: A 2012 investigation by Iraq's Board of Supreme Audit into the central bank's daily dollar auctions found most transactions were based on fraudulent paperwork; the top auditor told US officials that up to $800 million a week was leaving Iraq illegally, according to the US Special Inspector General for Iraq Reconstruction.
cases.source_title: Iraqi audit indicates money laundering, US says (AP via Boston Globe)

cases.people: David Oddsson (former central bank head); Eirikur Gudnason and Ingimundur Fridriksson (central bank officials)
cases.summary: In April 2010 the parliament's Special Investigation Commission found that seven officials, including central bank head Oddsson and central bank officials Gudnason and Fridriksson, acted with gross negligence before the 2008 collapse of Iceland's three largest banks, failing to act on information about the banks' condition.
cases.source_title: Iceland parliament committee implicates former PM, bank chief in banking crisis (JURIST)

cases.people: Antonio Fazio (former governor); Gianpiero Fiorani (Banca Popolare di Lodi)
cases.summary: On 28 May 2011 a Milan court sentenced former governor Fazio to four years in prison and a €1.5 million fine for market rigging (aggiotaggio) in the 2005 attempted takeover of Antonveneta by Banca Popolare di Lodi; prosecutors argued he repeatedly favoured Fiorani's bank over ABN Amro by speeding some authorisations and slowing others. Later appeal outcomes were not checked for this record.
cases.source_title: Il caso Antonveneta (Il Post)

cases.people: Antonio Fazio (former governor) and 12 others
cases.summary: Fazio was sentenced in October 2011 to three and a half years at first instance over Unipol's attempted 2005 takeover of BNL; on 30 May 2012 the Milan Court of Appeal acquitted him and 12 other defendants of market rigging.
cases.source_title: La sentenza su Unipol e BNL (Il Post)

cases.people: Toshihiko Fukui (governor 2003-2008)
cases.summary: In June 2006 Fukui apologised and took a 30% pay cut for six months after disclosing he had kept a 10 million yen investment, made in 1999, in a fund run by Yoshiaki Murakami, who was arrested for insider trading; the stake had grown to 22 million yen. The BoJ said he broke no law or internal rule; he did not resign.
cases.source_title: Bank of Japan chief apologizes for scandal (AP via NBC News)

cases.people: Eric Kotut (governor); Eliphaz Riungu (deputy governor); Wilfred Koinange (Treasury PS); Kamlesh Pattni (Goldenberg International)
cases.summary: In March 2006 Kenyan prosecutors indicted five people, including former governor Kotut and former deputy governor Riungu, over the Goldenberg scandal, in which the government paid cash subsidies for fictitious gold and diamond exports by Goldenberg International under President Moi. A judicial inquiry had reported in February 2006; earlier proceedings against Riungu had been halted.
cases.source_title: Top officials charged in fraud scandal (Mail & Guardian)

cases.people: Andrew Mullei (governor); Silla Mullei (son)
cases.summary: On 23 March 2006 governor Mullei was charged with four counts of abuse of office, including appointing his son as a CBK consultant without following procurement procedures, under which the son was paid Sh2,619,154.85 in consultancy fees, and improperly appointing three other consultants; he denied awarding Sh9 million in contracts irregularly and was freed on Sh5 million bail.
cases.source_title: CBK governor charged with abuse of office (Central Banking)

cases.people: Unnamed former and current CBK officials
cases.summary: Kenya's Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission said it was investigating former and current CBK officials over their role in the accounting fraud that brought down Imperial Bank. Imperial Bank's directors told a parliamentary committee in August 2018 that CBK officers took part in the Sh34 billion embezzlement by manipulating the bank's IT systems.
cases.source_title: Probe turns to CBK staff linked to collapse of Imperial, Chase banks (Business Daily)

cases.central_bank: National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic
cases.people: Ulan Sarbanov (governor)
cases.summary: In September 2005 prosecutors placed governor Sarbanov under house arrest, accusing him of abuse of power for handing out more than $400,000 to deposed president Askar Akayev in 1999. Sarbanov denied wrongdoing.
cases.source_title: Kyrgyzstan's central bank chief under house arrest (Central Banking)

cases.people: Khamphout (former director general, Monetary Policy Department); Aod (former director general, Banking Operations Department)
cases.summary: On 8 September 2026 the Vientiane People's Court sentenced two former Bank of the Lao PDR directors general to life imprisonment (Aod in absentia; he died during proceedings) for abusing their positions to withdraw foreign currency from the central bank's reserves and exchange unlimited amounts; in a related case nine bank employees were convicted of corruption and money laundering including trading currency at special rates. Losses across the cases exceeded 2.29 trillion kip ($102.6 million).
cases.source_title: Lao central bank employees sent to jail over corruption charges (Vientiane Times/ANN via The Star)

cases.people: Riad Salameh (governor)
cases.summary: In May 2023 French prosecutors issued an arrest warrant for Salameh after he failed to appear for questioning in a probe by a French, German and Luxembourg judicial team into illicit enrichment and alleged laundering of $330 million; Germany issued a second warrant the following week on charges including corruption, forgery, money laundering and embezzlement. Salameh called the French warrant a violation of the law.
cases.source_title: France issues arrest warrant for Lebanon's central bank chief (Al Jazeera)

cases.people: Riad Salameh (governor); Raja Salameh (brother, controller of Forry Associates)
cases.summary: Salameh has been investigated over allegations that more than $300 million was siphoned off between 2002 and 2015 through Forry Associates, a company controlled by his brother Raja and suspected of receiving commissions from commercial banks and transferring them abroad. The central bank said it would act as principal plaintiff in the state investigation; investigations are also open in France, Germany, Switzerland and other countries. Both brothers deny wrongdoing.
cases.source_title: Lebanon charges ex-central bank governor Salameh over alleged $44.8 million embezzlement (Reuters, via Al-Monitor)

cases.people: Riad Salameh (governor 1993-2023); lawyers Marwan Issa el-Khoury and Michel John Tueni
cases.summary: In January 2026 Beirut's indictment chamber indicted Salameh and two lawyers on charges including embezzlement of public funds, forgery and illicit enrichment, accusing them of embezzling $44.8 million from a central bank 'consultancy account'. Salameh had been detained about 13 months and released in September 2025 on bail of more than $14 million; he denies wrongdoing.
cases.source_title: Lebanon charges ex-central bank governor Salameh over alleged $44.8 million embezzlement (Reuters, via Al-Monitor)

cases.people: Riad Salameh (governor); members of the Central Council
cases.summary: The Alvarez & Marsal forensic audit (2023) found that BdL's foreign-currency position went from a $7.2 billion surplus at end-2015 to a $50.7 billion deficit at end-2020 while 'no loss is shown at all in the balance sheet', with losses netted or recorded in general accounts; it found Salameh set accounting standards that concealed losses and decided which banks benefited from financial engineering, and that the Central Council did not challenge him.
cases.source_title: Alvarez & Marsal delivers damning report on Lebanon's central bank (Consultancy-me)

cases.people: Riad Salameh (governor)
cases.summary: BdL's 2018 audited accounts, signed off with qualifications by EY and Deloitte, recorded a $6.82 billion asset described as 'seigniorage on financial stability', inflating assets by over $6 billion while the bank helped fund a widening government deficit; the amount was determined yearly by the governor.
cases.source_title: Lebanon: Central bank chief inflated assets by $6bn in 2018 (Reuters via Al Jazeera)

cases.people: Mazen Hamdan (director of cash operations)
cases.summary: On 18 May 2020 Lebanese prosecutor Ali Ibrahim charged Mazen Hamdan, the central bank's director of cash operations, with illegally manipulating the exchange rate, after ordering his arrest on 14 May, according to a judicial source cited by AFP.
cases.source_title: Lebanese central bank official arrested over currency allegations (Central Banking)

cases.people: Charles Sirleaf (deputy governor); Milton Weeks (governor); Dorbor Hagba (director of banking)
cases.summary: In March 2019 a Monrovia court ordered former deputy governor Sirleaf, former governor Weeks and official Hagba held for trial on charges of economic sabotage, misuse of public money, theft or illegal disbursement of public money and criminal conspiracy over Liberian dollar banknotes printed in 2016-2018 that could not be accounted for. AFP later reported that the Justice Minister dropped charges against Sirleaf and three others while Weeks remained under indictment.
cases.source_title: Ex-Liberian president's son charged over missing money scandal (Al Jazeera)

cases.people: Jolue Aloysius Tarlue (governor)
cases.summary: In July 2024 Liberia suspended governor Tarlue indefinitely after a General Auditing Commission report on 2018-2023 found irregularities in central bank lending to the government, including more than $80 million in apparently unauthorised financing for salary payments, irregular contract awards and management exceeding approved expenditure limits.
cases.source_title: Liberia suspends central bank governor over audit (Reuters via Polity)

cases.people: Arjuna Mahendran (former governor) and 9 others including Arjun Aloysius (Perpetual Treasuries)
cases.summary: In June 2019 the Attorney General filed an indictment with 23 counts under the Public Property Act and the Registered Stocks and Securities Ordinance against former governor Mahendran and nine others before a three-judge Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar, over the February 2015 treasury bond auction. The Special High Court later issued an arrest warrant for Mahendran.
cases.source_title: AG filed indictment against Mahendran and 9 others before Special HC (Ada Derana)

cases.people: Ajith Nivard Cabraal and W.D. Lakshman (former governors); members of the Monetary Board; Gotabaya, Mahinda and Basil Rajapaksa
cases.summary: On 14 November 2023 a majority of a five-judge Supreme Court bench ruled that the three Rajapaksa brothers, former governors Cabraal and Lakshman, the former finance secretary, the former presidential secretary and members of the central bank's Monetary Board violated the public trust and breached Article 12(1) of the Constitution in their administration of the economy, leading to the 2022 economic crisis.
cases.source_title: Gotabaya, Mahinda, Basil & others responsible for economic crisis - SC rules (Ada Derana)

cases.people: Ilmārs Rimšēvičs (former governor); Māris Martinsons (businessman)
cases.summary: On 20 December 2023 the Riga District Court convicted former governor Rimšēvičs of accepting a bribe and other material inducements and sentenced him to six years in prison with a five-year ban on public office; about €25,000 and several properties were confiscated. He was tried alongside businessman Māris Martinsons.
cases.source_title: Latvian ex-governor Rimšēvičs sentenced to six years in prison (Central Banking)

cases.people: Dorin Drăguțanu (governor 2009-2016); Aureliu Cincilei (deputy governor); Emma Tăbîrţă (former deputy governor 2008-2015); Ion Ropot (head of bank resolution division)
cases.summary: On 5 March 2020 Moldovan prosecutors searched National Bank headquarters and detained deputy governor Cincilei, former deputy governor Tăbîrţă and a division head on suspicion of participating in fraud and money laundering linked to the theft of about $1 billion from three banks that surfaced in 2014-2015, when the central bank extended a MDL13 billion emergency loan later converted into public debt; prosecutors moved to arrest former governor Drăguțanu.
cases.source_title: Moldovan central bank officials arrested over $1bn bank frauds (bne IntelliNews)

cases.people: Rogelio Ramírez de la O (finance minister, attends Banxico board meetings); President Andrés Manuel López Obrador
cases.summary: On 23 March 2022 President López Obrador announced Banxico's unanimous rate rise from 6% to 6.5% before the central bank published it; on 25 March he said the finance minister, who takes part in Banxico board meetings, had informed him the previous evening, apologised to the governor and accepted that they had violated the Banco de México law. Deputy governor Gerardo Esquivel called it an error, not a leak.
cases.source_title: AMLO revela quién le informó por adelantado el aumento de tasa de Banxico (El Financiero)

cases.people: Harvesh Seegolam (former governor); Renganaden Padayachy (former finance minister)
cases.summary: On 9-10 April 2025 Mauritius's Financial Crimes Commission arrested former governor Seegolam for 'fraud by abuse of position' and he was charged with fraud and released on bail, in the investigation into the alleged embezzlement of 300 million rupees ($6.7 million) from the Mauritius Investment Corporation, a central bank-owned vehicle set up during the COVID pandemic. Seegolam and Padayachy deny wrongdoing.
cases.source_title: Former Mauritius central bank governor charged with fraud, freed on bail (Reuters via Yahoo)

cases.people: Dalitso Kabambe (governor); Henry Mathanga (deputy governor for operations); Rodrick Wiyo (director of financial markets operations); Leah Donga (senior dealer)
cases.summary: After a forensic audit of RBM payments between January 2019 and June 2020, the state charged the four with abuse of office, negligence, money laundering and causing loss of public funds, alleging payment of K4.3 billion to FDH Bank without board approval. Pleas were not taken as charges were subject to change.
cases.source_title: Kabambe, 3 others charged, bail ruling today (Nation Online)

cases.people: Dalitso Kabambe (governor); Joseph Mwanamvekha (finance minister)
cases.summary: In December 2021 Malawi police arrested Kabambe and Mwanamvekha; police said they procured and masterminded the falsification of Gross Liability and Net Reserve Base returns to make the IMF believe Malawi was meeting Extended Credit Facility conditions.
cases.source_title: Malawi nabs 2 ex-ministers, governor (AFP via Manila Times)

cases.people: Unnamed officials of the note-issuing authority; bribe payers: Securency and NPA
cases.summary: In October 2011 Securency and NPA (subsidiaries of the Reserve Bank of Australia) pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials to obtain banknote business with the note-issuing authority of Malaysia between 2001-2003. The officials are not named in the RBA chronology.
cases.source_title: Chronology: Events related to charges against Note Printing Australia and Securency (Reserve Bank of Australia)

cases.people: Mohamad Daud Dol Moin (Bank Negara official, retired 2009)
cases.summary: Former Bank Negara official Mohamad Daud was charged by the MACC in July 2011 with receiving two RM50,000 bribes in 2004-2005 linked to the RM95 million RM5 polymer note contract won by Note Printing Australia. The Shah Alam Sessions Court acquitted him without calling his defence on 6 December 2015, and the Attorney-General withdrew the appeal in February 2016.
cases.source_title: The Mohamad Daud Dol Moin story (The Edge Malaysia)

cases.people: Charles Soludo (governor May 2004-May 2009) and other top CBN officials
cases.summary: In an AFP report (IOL shows it as published about 13 years ago, i.e. around 2013), Nigeria's EFCC said it had questioned former governor Soludo in a probe into allegations that Securency, part-owned by the Reserve Bank of Australia, bribed top CBN officials to win the contract to print polymer banknotes between 2006 and 2008.
cases.source_title: Nigeria probes banknote graft (AFP via IOL)

cases.people: Godwin Emefiele (governor 2014-2023)
cases.summary: The December 2023 report of special investigator Jim Obazee on the CBN, submitted to President Tinubu, said Emefiele kept billions of naira in 593 bank accounts in the US, UK and China and placed £543,482,213 in UK fixed deposits without approval of the CBN board or investment committee.
cases.source_title: Emefiele illegally kept funds in 593 US, UK, China accounts, says probe panel (TheCable)

cases.people: Godwin Emefiele (governor)
cases.summary: In January 2024 Emefiele was re-arraigned by the EFCC on 20 counts including conspiracy, criminal breach of trust, forgery and obtaining money by false pretences, including awarding a 2018 contract for Toyota Hilux vehicles to a company linked to bank staff and obtaining over $6 million by falsely claiming the president directed an advance. He pleaded not guilty.
cases.source_title: Former Nigeria central bank governor re-arraigned on expanded corruption charges (JURIST)

cases.people: Godwin Emefiele (governor); Henry Isioma Omole (co-defendant)
cases.summary: In April 2024 the EFCC filed a 26-count charge in Lagos alleging Emefiele directed allocation of $2,136,391,737.33 of foreign exchange without bids and made other unbid allocations in 2020-2021; co-defendant Omole is accused of receiving a $110,000 bribe on Emefiele's behalf for favourable allocations.
cases.source_title: Emefiele faces trial for alleged $2.14bn forex abuse in Lagos on Monday (BusinessDay)

cases.people: Godwin Emefiele (governor)
cases.summary: In April 2024 the EFCC filed a four-count charge accusing Emefiele of approving the printing of N684,590,000 in banknotes at a cost of N18.96 billion during the 2022-2023 naira redesign and of unlawfully approving withdrawal of N124.8 billion from the federation's consolidated revenue fund.
cases.source_title: 'He printed N684.5m notes with N18.9bn' -- EFCC to arraign Emefiele on fresh charge (TheCable)

cases.people: Togun Kayode Philip (senior clerk, CBN Ibadan branch) and Wema Bank staff
cases.summary: A CBN senior clerk and a Wema Bank employee were sentenced to three years each after a plea bargain with the EFCC on six counts of stealing and conspiracy, part of the N8 billion currency mutilation scam at the CBN Ibadan branch.
cases.source_title: Court Sentences Two, Orders Forfeiture of Property over N8bn Currency Scam (ThisDay via AELEX)

cases.people: Unnamed officials of the note-issuing authority; bribe payers: NPA
cases.summary: In October 2011 NPA (subsidiaries of the Reserve Bank of Australia) pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials to obtain banknote business with the note-issuing authority of Nepal between 2000-2002. The officials are not named in the RBA chronology.
cases.source_title: Chronology: Events related to charges against Note Printing Australia and Securency (Reserve Bank of Australia)

cases.people: Bijaya Nath Bhattarai (governor); Surendra Man Pradhan (executive director, Financial Institutions Regulation Department)
cases.summary: In 2007 Nepal's Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority charged sitting governor Bhattarai and executive director Pradhan with embezzlement over the hiring of American consultants for the second phase of the Financial Sector Reform Program, and Bhattarai was suspended. The Supreme Court later cleared both, allowing Bhattarai's reinstatement; a confidential World Bank report reported in 2014 named a private banker as the main figure behind the scandal.
cases.source_title: SC gives clean chit to NRB ex-guv; Kshetry's future uncertain (myRepublica)

cases.people: Maha Prasad Adhikari (governor)
cases.summary: On 8 April 2022 the government suspended governor Adhikari and formed a three-member probe committee headed by a former Supreme Court judge over charges of leaking sensitive information about government decisions and not fulfilling his responsibilities. On 19 April 2022 the Supreme Court stayed the suspension and he returned to work.
cases.source_title: Governor Adhikari suspended on charge of leaking sensitive information (Kathmandu Post)

cases.people: Unnamed senior SBP officials including an executive director
cases.summary: In August 2025 Pakistan Observer reported, citing internal memos and cash slips, that senior State Bank of Pakistan officials including an executive director allegedly issued bulk fresh banknotes directly to private brokers, who resold them at premiums, with each transaction netting officials at least Rs2 million in kickbacks; it said no probe had been opened.
cases.source_title: Fresh Eid Notes diverted by SBP Officials to Brokers in New Scam: report (Pakistan Observer)

cases.people: Elizabeth Genia (acting governor, appointed governor in 2024)
cases.summary: Court documents obtained by OCCRP show the National Fraud and Anti-Corruption Directorate searched Bank of PNG offices in August-September 2023 in a money-laundering investigation into then-acting governor Genia, who obtained a temporary stay that was later dismissed; she was appointed governor in early 2024 and has not been charged. She had also previously been under fraud-squad investigation over a firearms deal for the bank's security team.
cases.source_title: PNG Central Bank Chief Appointed Amid Money Laundering Investigation (OCCRP)

cases.people: Bogdan Olteanu (deputy governor; Chamber of Deputies speaker at the time of the alleged offence)
cases.summary: In 2014 Romania's High Court of Cassation and Justice placed sitting BNR deputy governor Olteanu under 30-day house arrest in a National Anticorruption Directorate case alleging he asked for and received a €1 million bribe in 2008, while parliament speaker, from businessman Sorin Ovidiu Vântu; his lawyer said he would resign from the BNR. The outcome of the trial was not checked for this record.
cases.source_title: Central bank deputy governor placed under house arrest in million-euro bribery case (Antena 3 / Agerpres)

cases.people: Alexei Mishin (chief legal expert, Moscow directorate of the Central Bank); Oleg Alexeyev (Federal Tax Service)
cases.summary: On 19 October 2005 the Moscow prosecutor's office indicted Alexei Mishin, chief legal expert at the Central Bank's Moscow directorate, and a deputy department head of the Federal Tax Service for accepting a $1 million bribe, according to Interfax.
cases.source_title: Russian central banker charged with taking bribe (Central Banking)

cases.people: Philip Bobongi (central bank employee)
cases.summary: Former central bank employee Bobongi was sentenced to nine years after being convicted on 39 counts of money laundering and two counts of larceny and embezzlement for stealing more than $1.7 million in old banknotes in 2007-2009 while the bank was destroying them.
cases.source_title: Former Central Bank employee jailed for embezzlement (SIBC)

cases.people: The central bank governor in office in mid-2013 (referred to as 'the current governor'; name not given in the article read)
cases.summary: A July 2013 report by the UN Monitoring Group for Somalia and Eritrea said 80% of withdrawals from the Central Bank were made for private purposes, and that the governor was key to irregularities, with $12 million of $16.9 million transferred by PricewaterhouseCoopers untraceable. The central bank rejected the allegations.
cases.source_title: UN experts say corruption still rampant in Somalia (AP via The Jakarta Post)

cases.people: Yussur Abrar (governor, September-October 2013)
cases.summary: Governor Abrar resigned after seven weeks, writing to the president that from her appointment she had 'continuously been asked to sanction deals and violate my fiduciary responsibility'; she had refused to sanction a contract over frozen government assets with US law firm Shulman Rogers, which denied wrongdoing.
cases.source_title: Somalia: Head of Central Bank Resigns Citing Corruption (OCCRP)

cases.people: Dejan Simić (vice-governor)
cases.summary: In January 2006 Serbian police arrested National Bank vice-governor Dejan Simić on suspicion of taking bribes, according to the Mina news agency. The outcome was not checked for this record.
cases.source_title: Serbia's National Bank vice-governor arrested (Central Banking)

cases.people: Emmanuel Makuach Ayuel (consultant, Bank of South Sudan); De La Rue (banknote printer)
cases.summary: A UN Human Rights Council commission report said De La Rue transferred about $1.4 million to an Equity Bank account in Nairobi held by a Bank of South Sudan consultant between 2016 and September 2017, against a banknote contract worth about $144 million, and noted 'suspected corruption'. The UK Serious Fraud Office closed its own investigation in June 2020 without charges.
cases.source_title: Kenyan bank link in South Sudan bribery (Daily Nation)

cases.people: Moses Makur Deng Manguak (governor January-August 2022)
cases.summary: In February-March 2026 South Sudanese security forces detained former governor Manguak (placed under house arrest) with former finance ministers and other officials; the information minister said a committee was investigating 'financial malpractices'. No charges had been publicly announced as of March 2026, and Manguak denies the allegations.
cases.source_title: Corruption-Linked Arrests in South Sudan Raise Questions (Human Rights Watch)

cases.people: Gillmore Hoefdraad (central bank governor 2010-2015, finance minister 2015-2020)
cases.summary: On 17 December 2021 a Surinamese court sentenced Hoefdraad in absentia to 12 years and a S$500,000 fine on corruption charges, as part of a conspiracy to defraud the central bank while he was finance minister. On appeal on 19 January 2026 the court imposed 10 years for violating the anti-corruption law and embezzlement, dropping the criminal-organisation count; Hoefdraad, who left Suriname in 2020, called the case a political show trial.
cases.source_title: Surinaams hof verlaagt straffen voormalige financiële top (ANP via Welingelichte Kringen)

cases.people: Robert van Trikt (governor 2019-2020); Faranaaz Alibaks-Hausil (head of legal affairs); Ginmardo Kromosoeto (Postspaarbank director); Ashween Angnoe
cases.summary: On 31 January 2022 a court convicted former governor van Trikt of violating the Anti-Corruption Act, forgery, embezzlement, money laundering and participation in a criminal enterprise in a case involving over $800,000 to the detriment of the central bank, sentencing him to eight years and a S$500,000 fine; the central bank's legal director and others were also convicted. On appeal in January 2026 his sentence was reduced to six years.
cases.source_title: Six Years in Prison for Central Bank Governor (Caribbean National Weekly)

cases.people: Peter Kažimír (governor; finance minister at the time of the offence)
cases.summary: On 29 May 2025 the Specialised Criminal Court found sitting governor Kažimír guilty of paying a €48,000 bribe in 2017-2018, while finance minister, to the head of the tax office in connection with audits of private companies, and fined him €200,000. He denied wrongdoing and said he would appeal; the offence predates his central bank post.
cases.source_title: Slovakia's PM slams judge over conviction of central bank boss (Al Jazeera)

cases.people: A small number of unnamed Riksbank employees
cases.summary: On 18 June 2021 the Riksbank stated that a routine check of staff securities dealings found a few employees had made transactions not in line with its ethics rules, including share trades close to monetary policy decisions and share trades in companies whose corporate bonds the Riksbank was buying for monetary policy purposes; it called this inappropriate, held talks with those involved and began revising the rules.
cases.source_title: Riksbanken reviderar interna etiska regler efter överträdelser (Sveriges Riksbank)

cases.people: Stefan Ingves (governor); Cecilia Skingsley (first deputy governor)
cases.summary: After media reports that Ingves and Skingsley had conflicts of interest from share holdings when deciding on secondary-market corporate bond purchases, the Riksbank's General Council reviewed the matter and on 17 December 2021 concluded that the link between their holdings and their participation in decisions was too weak to constitute a conflict of interest and found no shortcoming in their conduct.
cases.source_title: Riksbanksfullmäktige finner inget jäv i samband med penningpolitiska beslut (Sveriges Riksbank)

cases.people: Unnamed decision makers at the Central Bank of Syria
cases.summary: A Vienna court found that Austrian banknote printer OeBS overcharged the Central Bank of Syria by 14% on banknote contracts and that the kickback returned to local decision makers; OeBS managers were convicted in 2014 and on retrial in 2018. No Syrian official was named or tried in these proceedings.
cases.source_title: Verdicts in the OeBS kickback affair (CoinsWeekly)

cases.people: National Bank of Tajikistan management (unnamed)
cases.summary: In March 2008 the IMF Executive Board found that the National Bank of Tajikistan had supplied inaccurate information on the cotton sector, international reserves, net domestic assets and credit policy, including reporting reserves of about $450 million when they were roughly one-third of that and concealing that reserves were pledged as collateral for loans to the cotton sector; Tajikistan was required to repay $47.4 million.
cases.source_title: Tajikistan: IMF Catches Dushanbe in Creative Accounting Scandal (Eurasianet)

cases.people: Khudaiberdi Orazov (central bank chairman 1992-1998)
cases.summary: In March 2002 Turkmenistan's prosecutor's office accused former central bank chairman Orazov of embezzling $120 million in German and Swiss loans, according to Interfax.
cases.source_title: Ex-Turkmenistan banker accused of loan fraud (Central Banking)

cases.people: Five central bank agents including two cashiers (unnamed)
cases.summary: In February 2018 Tunisian prosecutors said five Banque Centrale de Tunisie agents were arrested, two of them jailed, in a currency-trafficking investigation, accused of money laundering, corruption and abuse of power for exchanging small euro notes for €200 and €500 notes without recording the operations; the central bank said it had referred the illegal operations to the courts itself.
cases.source_title: Tunisie : des agents de la Banque centrale arrêtés pour blanchiment et corruption (TSA / AFP)

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
cases.people: Emrah Şener (former deputy governor); Baran Aytaş (former CEO of Interbank Card Center, BKM)
cases.summary: In October 2025 Istanbul prosecutors took former central bank deputy governor Şener and six others into custody, and he was arrested, in a corruption and tender-rigging investigation into two 2023 tenders at the Interbank Card Center (BKM), the national payment network in which the central bank holds a majority stake.
cases.source_title: Former Turkish Central Bank deputy governor arrested for fraud at state-backed payment body (Turkish Minute)

cases.people: Daudi Ballali (governor)
cases.summary: An Ernst & Young audit of the Bank of Tanzania's External Payment Arrears (EPA) account found about Sh133 billion paid wrongly to 22 local companies, many phoney or using fake documents, in 2005/06; President Kikwete dismissed governor Ballali in January 2008. Companies were ordered to refund money and some lower-level defendants were jailed.
cases.source_title: How corruption rocked Kikwete's govt in the past decade (The Citizen)

cases.people: Emmanuel Tumusiime-Mutebile (governor) and senior directors
cases.summary: A confidential 2018 Auditor General report to parliament said Bank of Uganda managers, including governor Mutebile, acted without guidelines, regulations or policies and may have intentionally neglected aspects of the closure and sale of at least seven commercial banks, including Crane Bank (2016-2017).
cases.source_title: BoU top officials in panic as AG report exposes dirt in sale of banks (Eagle Online)

cases.people: Oleksandr Pysaruk (first deputy governor 2014-2015) and other current and former NBU officials
cases.summary: On 11 November 2019 Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau detained seven people, including former NBU first deputy governor Pysaruk and current and former NBU officials, on suspicion of embezzling UAH1.2 billion (about $49 million) of a 2014 NBU stabilisation loan to VAB Bank, which was declared insolvent in November 2014.
cases.source_title: Ukraine main anti-graft agency detains former central bank governor's deputy (bne IntelliNews)

cases.people: Jeffrey Lacker (president, Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond)
cases.summary: In April 2017 Lacker resigned with immediate effect, stating that in October 2012 he spoke with a Medley Global Advisors analyst who held confidential information on options discussed at the September 2012 FOMC meeting and that he may have confirmed it, and that he had not disclosed this in a 2012 internal inquiry. His lawyer said the investigation was complete and no charges would be brought.
cases.source_title: Richmond Fed Head Resigns, Admits Leaking (AP via Courthouse News)

cases.people: Raphael Bostic (president, Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta)
cases.summary: A Fed Inspector General report issued 11 September 2024 found that trades made on Bostic's behalf over about five years from 2017, including several during FOMC blackout periods, violated Fed ethics policies and 'created the appearance' of acting on confidential information and of a conflict of interest, but found no violation of federal insider trading or conflict of interest laws.
cases.source_title: Atlanta Fed official broke ethics rules but didn't violate insider trading laws, probe finds (AP via WABE)

cases.people: Jerome Powell (chair); Richard Clarida (vice chair)
cases.summary: The Fed Inspector General investigated Powell's December 2019 and Clarida's 2020 trades and did not find evidence that either violated laws, rules or policies then in effect, while stating that those rules 'did not sufficiently support public confidence'. No referral for law enforcement was made.
cases.source_title: Report of Investigation on the Closing of 22-0028-I Board Trading Activity (Federal Reserve OIG)

cases.people: Robert Kaplan (president, Dallas Fed); Eric Rosengren (president, Boston Fed)
cases.summary: The Fed Inspector General's January 2024 report found that Kaplan's 2020 trading created an 'appearance of acting on confidential FOMC information' and an 'appearance of a conflict of interest', and that Rosengren failed to report multiple trades and that his 2020 REIT trades created an 'appearance of a conflict of interest'.
cases.source_title: Report of Investigation on the Closing of 22-0030-I Reserve Bank Trading Activity (Federal Reserve OIG)

cases.people: Adriana Kugler (Fed governor, stepped down 8 August 2025)
cases.summary: A report released on 15 November 2025 by the US Office of Government Ethics, after a Fed referral to its inspector general, showed that Kugler's 2024 financial disclosure listed more than a dozen individual stock trades, several during FOMC blackout periods, which violated Fed rules barring officials from holding individual stocks; the largest was an April 2024 Apple purchase of $100,000-$250,000.
cases.source_title: Former Fed governor's stock trades violated the central bank's ethics rules (AP via ClickOnDetroit)

cases.people: Unnamed officials of the note-issuing authority; bribe payers: Securency
cases.summary: In October 2011 Securency (subsidiaries of the Reserve Bank of Australia) pleaded guilty in the Supreme Court of Victoria to conspiring to provide benefits to foreign public officials to obtain banknote business with the note-issuing authority of Vietnam between 2001-2004. The officials are not named in the RBA chronology.
cases.source_title: Chronology: Events related to charges against Note Printing Australia and Securency (Reserve Bank of Australia)

cases.people: Do Thi Nhan (head banking inspector); Nguyen Van Hung (deputy chief inspector)
cases.summary: In April 2024 Ho Chi Minh City People's Court sentenced Van Thinh Phat chair Truong My Lan to death for fraud at Saigon Commercial Bank, finding she ordered subordinates to bribe State Bank of Vietnam inspectors; state media said head banking inspector Do Thi Nhan received $5.2 million in bribes and deputy chief inspector Nguyen Van Hung $300,000.
cases.source_title: Van Thinh Phat chairwoman sentenced to death in Vietnam's biggest fraud trial (Radio Free Asia)

cases.people: Central Bank of Yemen management (unnamed)
cases.summary: A January 2021 UN Panel of Experts report said the Aden-based central bank broke its foreign-exchange rules and laundered 'a substantial part' of a $2 billion Saudi deposit, giving traders a $423 million windfall; the bank rejected the claims. On 25 March 2021, after an internal review, the panel informed the government that it withdrew the money-laundering and corruption accusations, according to a Yemeni official quoted by Arab News.
cases.source_title: UN Report Accuses Yemen's Warring Sides of Corruption (OCCRP)

cases.people: South African Reserve Bank; Absa (successor to Bankorp)
cases.summary: In June 2017 the Public Protector ordered Absa to repay R1.125 billion for an apartheid-era Reserve Bank lifeboat to Bankorp. On 16 February 2018 the Pretoria High Court set aside the report and its remedial action on review applications by the Reserve Bank and Absa, and ordered the Public Protector to pay part of the Reserve Bank's costs personally.
cases.source_title: Public Protector's ABSA bailout report set aside (Mail & Guardian)

cases.people: Gideon Gono (governor 2003-2013)
cases.summary: Under Gono the RBZ ran 'quasi-fiscal' activities, including cash for state enterprises and farm equipment handed out at events presided over by President Mugabe, and raided private foreign-currency accounts to fund state operations, leaving debts of close to $1.3 billion. In 2014 the government tabled the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (Debt Assumption) Bill to move the debt to taxpayers.
cases.source_title: Taxpayers expected to rescue Zimbabwe's Reserve Bank (Mail & Guardian)

cases.people: Khuphukile Mlambo (RBZ deputy governor); Kudakwashe Tagwirei / Sakunda Holdings (recipient)
cases.summary: At a September 2019 Public Accounts Committee hearing, RBZ deputy governor Mlambo confirmed the central bank issued $663.8 million in Treasury Bills to Sakunda Holdings, owned by presidential ally Kudakwashe Tagwirei, in 2017-2018 for Command Agriculture on Finance Ministry instruction; the committee also cited a $1.37 billion overdraft issued by December 2017 without parliamentary approval and could not get an explanation for $2.9 billion paid from unallocated reserves in 2017.
cases.source_title: Parly queries 'rogue' RBZ payments (NewsDay via Nehanda Radio)

cases.people: Julio Suárez (president of Banguat, also vice president of the IGSS social security board)
cases.summary: In May 2015 Banguat president Julio Suárez was arrested with other members of the board of the social security institute (IGSS). Prosecutors said they took part in the irregular award of a 116 million quetzal (about $14.5 million) IGSS contract to the drug company Pisa de Guatemala; the charges listed for the detainees as a group were unlawful association, influence peddling, illegal commissions and active bribery. He was later acquitted: the Supreme Court's Criminal Chamber upheld the June 2019 appeal-court acquittal, as reported in October 2021.
cases.source_title: Arrestan a directores de banco central y seguridad social de Guatemala por corrupción (Teletica)
cases.update_title: Caso IGSS-Pisa: sentencia absolutoria es confirmada por la CSJ (La Hora)

cases.people: Head of the BCV Payments and Taxes Department and two Procurement and Supply staff (named in the source)
cases.summary: In January 2020 prosecutor Tarek William Saab said a BCV payments head and others forged procurement files so the bank paid about $1.7 million, in 7 payments, to three companies it had not contracted, for overpriced goods that were never delivered. Eight arrest warrants were requested on charges of illegal profit in public administration, diversion of public funds, criminal association and money laundering. The case began with a complaint by BCV president Calixto Ortega; the source reports no trial or conviction.
cases.source_title: Tarek William Saab devela trama de corrupción en el BCV (La Patilla)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: On 24 July 2012 three Banco Central de Chile staff allegedly tried to take about 38 million Chilean pesos in banknotes being processed for destruction; a fourth was detained the next day. The bank itself reported the case, passed it to the police economic crimes unit and began legal action. The source reports no outcome.
cases.source_title: Banco Central: un cuarto funcionario fue detenido por el intento de robo de billetes (Diario Financiero)

cases.people: none named
cases.summary: A special anti-money-laundering police unit searched the BCP on 13 July, after the bank's supervision authority declined to give prosecutors documents, citing bank secrecy laws. The authorities' probe concerns embezzlement and money laundering and is linked to the Fifa-gate investigations. The readable part of the source names no individuals and reports no charges.
cases.source_title: Police search Paraguay central bank (Central Banking)

cases.people: Luis Gonzalez Macchi (President of Paraguay)
cases.summary: In January 2003 impeachment proceedings began against President Luis González Macchi, accused among other things, according to Central Banking, of embezzling US$26m from the central bank. Later reports describe US$16m from two bankrupt private banks taken over by the state. In February 2003 the Senate vote fell short (25 of 44, with 30 needed). A court sentenced him to six years in June 2006, and an appeals court later cleared him, saying the evidence was insufficient.
cases.source_title: Central Banking article on the impeachment of President Gonzalez Macchi, 29 January 2003 (Central Banking)
cases.update_title: Paraguay's ex-president cleared of corruption (NBC News)

cases.people: Pedro Delgado (president of the BCE)
cases.summary: On 8 January 2019 Ecuador's National Court of Justice sentenced former BCE president Pedro Delgado to five years in prison, restitution of $788,855.94, forfeiture of assets and public apologies. The prosecutor's office described the crime as unlawful association, while the court's own post called it illicit enrichment. The same source reports a 2015 embezzlement (peculado) conviction carrying eight years, and says he allegedly allowed large loans without proper documents or guarantees while leading the bank.
cases.source_title: Pedro Delgado, condenado a cinco años de prisión por asociación ilícita (Expreso)

cases.people: Mario Alonso (former Central Bank president); Silvio Conrado (former Central Bank director); three other former directors (unnamed)
cases.summary: In 2007 Nicaragua's Comptroller General concluded that the Central Bank board sold CENI certificates, issued to cover the collapse of banks, for less than market value and then raised interest rates to benefit the main buyer, Bancentro; the fraud is described as $500 million. The Comptroller alleged criminal involvement by six men, including former finance minister Eduardo Montealegre, who denied wrongdoing and called it a political witch hunt. In July 2008 a special prosecutor filed charges against 39 people including Montealegre; that report names no central bank officials among the accused and gives no court ruling, and it says former Central Bank president Francisco Mayorga was already found guilty in the banking scandal.
cases.source_title: Montealegre implicated in banking certificate scandal (Tico Times)
cases.update_title: Montealegre, 38 others accused in Cenis case (Tico Times)

cases.central_bank: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR)
cases.people: Leonel Figueroa (former BCR president); Hector Neyra (former BCR general manager)
cases.summary: A 1991 New York grand-jury indictment of BCCI alleged $3 million in bribes in return for depositing part of Peru's 1986-87 reserves in BCCI's Panama branch; the BCR board approved moving $100 million and later doubling it. The indictment did not name BCR officials; the Christian Science Monitor identified Figueroa and Neyra in the matter, and both strenuously denied the charges, with Neyra calling the decision purely technical. All Peruvian deposits were withdrawn by the end of 1987.
cases.source_title: Peru Is Drawn Into Widening BCCI Scandal (Christian Science Monitor)

cases.people: Two Banco de la República department directors (named in the source)
cases.summary: Two Banco de la República officials were investigated for allegedly giving reserved information about people and companies to officials of the DAS security agency, and received a one-month suspension. In January 2011 the bank reported that the Procuraduría's second-instance ruling revoked the suspension, recognizing that they broke no rule.
cases.source_title: Satisfacción por fallo de la Procuraduría (Banco de la República)

cases.people: none named
cases.summary: After the ECCB seized the Stanford-owned Bank of Antigua, the Official Stanford Investors Committee sued it in Dallas in 2013, alleging it fraudulently misappropriated assets belonging to Stanford's victims and creditors. On 17 August 2018 a US federal judge dismissed the claims in full because the ECCB and Antigua are immune under US foreign sovereign immunity law. The court did not rule on whether the allegations were true.
cases.source_title: The Official Stanford Investors Committee v. Bank of Antigua et al, Memorandum Opinion and Order (US District Court, N.D. Texas)

cases.people: Christodoulos Christodoulou (former governor)
cases.summary: A EUR 1 million transfer from Focus Maritime Corporation in 2007, a few months after Christodoulou's term as governor expired, was not declared in accounts from 2007 to 2009. In 2014 he pleaded guilty to six tax offences and was given five months in prison. He had said he had not been bribed.
cases.source_title: CYPRUS: Ex central bank chief gets 5 months for tax fraud (Financial Mirror)

cases.people: Christodoulos Christodoulou (former governor)
cases.summary: Prosecutors charged Christodoulou and five others with corruption, money laundering and abuse of office over a EUR 1 million payment made in 2007 by a Greek businessman. On 31 July 2020 judges ended the trial, ruling that prosecutors should not have tried him twice over the alleged bribe payment.
cases.source_title: Cypriot judges end second trial of ex-governor (Central Banking)

cases.people: Edward Scicluna (governor; former finance minister)
cases.summary: Scicluna, governor and former finance minister, pleaded not guilty on 29 May 2024 to fraud and other financial crimes over the government's handling of a private hospital contract (the Vitals concession) while he was finance minister. He stepped aside as governor in July 2024 and was reinstated in July 2025 after the European Central Bank was consulted and raised no objections. These pages don't say how the case stands now.
cases.source_title: Maltese governor pleads not guilty to fraud (Central Banking)
cases.update_title: Malta, ex Finance Minister Scicluna reinstated as Central Bank Governor (Italpress)

cases.people: Miguel Ángel Fernández Ordóñez (former governor)
cases.summary: On 15 September 2017 Spain's National Court decided by majority, on an appeal filed by two trade unions, not to prosecute the former governor over the failure of the commercial bank Bankia in summer 2012. The decision was described as final.
cases.source_title: Spanish ex-governor will not face charges over Bankia case (Central Banking)

cases.people: Manuel de la Concha (former stock exchange syndic, convicted); Mariano Rubio (former governor, account holder; the report does not say he was charged)
cases.summary: In 2002 a Madrid court sentenced De la Concha to six years in prison for falsifying public documents linked to a securities account of former governor Mariano Rubio that he ran from his office. The report says a company already wound up, NALVI, was used from at least 1986 to hide Rubio as the investor. The ruling could be appealed.
cases.source_title: Report on De la Concha's six-year sentence, 4 July 2002 (Diario de León)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: In 2026 police arrested a long-time Czech National Bank employee accused of misappropriating tens of millions of koruna. The bank confirmed the theft was investigated at its Brno branch, after suspicious transactions on the man's account were flagged.
cases.source_title: Czech National Bank employee arrested for alleged theft (Central Banking)

cases.people: Siim Kallas (former president of the Bank of Estonia); Urmas Kaju (former adviser to the Bank of Estonia)
cases.summary: On 5 March 1999 the Tallinn City Court found Kallas and Kaju not guilty of abuse of power and submitting false information, in a case over the loss of $10 million from the North Estonian Bank. A charge of preparing to embezzle had been dropped two weeks earlier.
cases.source_title: Kallas acquitted in $10 million case (Baltic Times)

cases.people: Jean-Claude Trichet (governor; director of the Treasury at the time); Jacques de Larosière (governor at the time, fellow accused)
cases.summary: Trichet was charged with spreading false information and publishing inexact accounts of the state-owned bank Crédit Lyonnais for 1991 to mid-1993, and prosecutors recommended a 10-month suspended sentence. In June 2003 judges cleared him, writing that he had only imprecise or incorrect information on the losses. Prosecutors had about 10 days to appeal. The report calls Jacques de Larosière, Banque de France governor at the time, a fellow accused but does not state the verdict for him.
cases.source_title: Trichet cleared of wrongdoing (Irish Times)

cases.people: Pat Neary (chief executive of the financial regulator; joined the Central Bank in 1971)
cases.summary: Neary said he would retire early over the regulator's handling of EUR 87 million in secret directors' loans at Anglo Irish Bank. An internal committee found the matter, discovered in January 2008, was not pursued, partly because a letter from Anglo went missing. Neary said he was not told until the finance minister raised it in December 2008.
cases.source_title: Financial regulator steps down over Anglo loans inquiry (Irish Times)

cases.people: Bank of Lithuania official who monitored Snoras (named in the source)
cases.summary: A central bank official who monitored Snoras bank was sacked in November 2011 and charged with letting Snoras conceal information from the central bank's leadership, including on assets in Swiss banks. A guilty verdict from March 2014 was annulled by a Vilnius court, which found no crime; that ruling can be appealed to the Supreme Court.
cases.source_title: Lithuanian court acquits central bank's official who monitored bankrupt Snoras (Lithuania Tribune)

cases.people: none named at the central bank
cases.summary: The Scheltema committee, set up by finance minister Wouter Bos, reported in June 2010 that De Nederlandsche Bank fell seriously short as supervisor of DSB bank. It missed flaws when licensing DSB in 2005 and was too patient afterwards, though the committee thought a different approach probably would not have prevented DSB's collapse.
cases.source_title: Commissie Scheltema: 'DNB schoot tekort bij toezicht op DSB' (Accountant.nl)

cases.people: Nicolai Tangen (hired as oil fund CEO)
cases.summary: In 2020 Norges Bank's Supervisory Council warned that the hire of Tangen to run the oil fund could carry a risk of breaking laws, rules and guidelines. It said he still appeared to be the main owner of AKO Capital with voting control, despite the bank saying he had cut those ties, and that the bank had not handled transparency about the applicant list as expected.
cases.source_title: Botched hire of oil fund CEO risks breaking the law, say supervisors (IPE)

cases.people: Adam Glapiński (NBP president)
cases.summary: Ruling coalition MPs filed a motion in March 2024 to send Glapiński to the State Tribunal, with eight accusations. They include bond purchases in 2020-2021 said to have indirectly financed the deficit by at least 144 billion zloty, and breaching the bank's political neutrality. A committee adopted its report on 9 October 2026; the Sejm must still decide, and the NBP calls the accusations entirely groundless.
cases.source_title: Ruch bez precedensu. Trybunał dla Adama Glapińskiego? Komisja zdecydowała (money.pl)

cases.people: Vítor Constâncio (governor during part of the period); Carlos Costa (governor from 2010)
cases.summary: A 600-page report by a committee the Banco de Portugal itself appointed, with technical support from Boston Consulting Group, pointed to failures in its supervision of Banco Espírito Santo going back to the start of the previous decade. Information on the Espírito Santo group and on BES's operations in Angola was reportedly not used. The bank twice refused parliament's request for the report, which was reported by Jornal de Negócios.
cases.source_title: Avaliação do Banco de Portugal ao caso BES aponta falhas na supervisão desde Constâncio (Observador)

cases.people: Boštjan Jazbec (former governor); Stanislava Zadravec Caprirolo (former vice governor); Janez Fabijan (former vice governor); Tomaž Čemažar (ran the bailout project)
cases.summary: Police investigators filed a second criminal complaint alleging abuse of office over the 2013 bank bailout, in which a EUR 960 million bail-in hit about 100,000 junior bondholders and shareholders. A 2016 attempt hit a dead end over procedural errors, and an EU court ruled the ECB's archives were violated. The specialised prosecutor has asked the court to investigate.
cases.source_title: New attempt to prosecute C-bankers over bank bailout (Slovenia Times)

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo
cases.people: Hashim Rexhepi (governor)
cases.summary: EU law enforcement officials arrested governor Hashim Rexhepi in July 2010 on suspicion of abusing his official position, accepting bribes, tax evasion, trading in influence and money laundering. A Eulex judge threw out all charges on December 12, and in January 2012 Eulex said its prosecutor would take no further action after it lost an appeal.
cases.source_title: Eulex drops corruption charges against former Kosovo governor (Central Banking)

cases.people: Radoje Žugić (governor)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: the NGO MANS said five payments totaling €4,100 went to accounts of relatives of governor Radoje Žugić between January 2017 and April 2018, with no data on their purpose.
