Žugić reportedly told the daily Dan that he did not act illegally and that aid to relatives of bank employees is not unprecedented. The source reports no finding on the claim.
cases.source_title: Sukob u vrhu Centralne banke Crne Gore (RFE/RL Balkan)

cases.people: Irena Radović (deputy governor for banking supervision)
cases.summary: In July 2018 the bank's Council, chaired by governor Radoje Žugić, reportedly found that deputy governor Irena Radović lacked the required expertise, put personal interest ahead of the public interest and disclosed business secrets, and the bank asked parliament to dismiss her. She called this retaliation for revealing secrets about the bank's operations, called the decision illegal and said she would sue. The findings come from an internal body in an open dispute and the source reports no court ruling on them.
cases.source_title: Sukob u vrhu Centralne banke Crne Gore (RFE/RL Balkan)

cases.people: Milo Djukanovic (prime minister); Igor Luksic (finance minister); Radoje Zugic (First Bank board member)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: in July 2012 the NGO MANS filed reports with Special Prosecutor Djurdjina Ivanovic alleging that First Bank received a €44 million state loan in 2008 that it could not repay and €192.2 million from state stock sales in 2009. MANS also alleged that the accused changed banking laws and fired Central Bank administrators so the Central Bank could not supervise First Bank. These are an NGO's reports to the prosecutor; the source reports no charge brought by prosecutors.
cases.source_title: Montenegro: Corruption Charges Against Top Politicians, First Bank and Central Bank Officials (OCCRP)

cases.people: Papuna Lezhava, Archil Mestvrishvili, Nikoloz Gagua (vice presidents); Giorgi Bakradze (advisor to the president); Natia Turnava (acting president, who did not resign)
cases.summary: The National Bank unfroze assets tied to Otar Partskhaladze, a former Prosecutor General sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury, arguing that Georgian citizens cannot be sanctioned without a Georgian court conviction. Three of its four vice presidents and an advisor submitted resignations over the decision. President Salome Zurabishvili criticized acting president Natia Turnava for reportedly changing the rules unilaterally; the source cites no court verdict or official finding.
cases.source_title: Top Georgian central bank officials resign over unfreezing of assets of sanctioned former prosecutor (bne IntelliNews)
cases.update_title: Scandal around ex-general prosecutor continues in Georgia; Vice-presidents leave the National Bank (JAMnews, 20 Sep 2023)

cases.people: Nana Keinishvili (National Bank Council member)
cases.summary: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office is investigating Council member Nana Keinishvili for possible unlawful involvement in business activities by a public official, after complaints from the management of crypto firm Bitexchange LLC, which the National Bank forwarded. The bank had fined Bitexchange; RFE/RL reported the fine at 572 million lari, and the bank did not disclose the amount. The investigation was ongoing as of October 2026.
cases.source_title: Georgia's Prosecutor's Office launches investigation into National Bank Council member (JAMnews)

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina
cases.people: Senad Softić (governor)
cases.summary: A criminal complaint accused governor Senad Softić of suspected wrongdoing in several cases, including a project to acquire an office building in Pale and a procedure to buy land in Sarajevo. The BiH Prosecutor's Office said in February 2023 that it had opened a case and was verifying the allegations. The central bank said examining allegations is not an investigation and that reports of one were untrue.
cases.source_title: Bosnia examining criminal complaints against c-bank governor (SeeNews)

cases.people: N. Zoljargal (former governor)
cases.summary: The anti-corruption agency IAAC arrested former governor N. Zoljargal on 29 November 2017 and said the case concerned the "Chinggis bond" and a price stabilizing programme, as part of a probe into the bank's 2012-2016 administration. A court released him with a travel ban, and prosecutors had not officially charged him. No later outcome was found.
cases.source_title: Former chief of Mongolia's Central Bank released on bail (News.MN)

cases.people: N. Zoljargal (central bank president)
cases.summary: News.MN reported in April 2020 that N. Zoljargal, then president of the central bank, was charged along with former MP B. Bolor and MPs D. Ganbat and D. Erdenebat with abuse of power over illegally transferring 49 percent of the Erdenet Mining Company. The source gives no outcome, and none was found.
cases.source_title: Q1 2020 case review, published 8 April 2020 (News.MN)

cases.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of Belarus
cases.people: head of the main directorate for currency and financial monitoring and his deputy (roles only)
cases.summary: Belarus's KGB said in December 2016 that a directorate head at the National Bank and his deputy were arrested over a bribe, reported as 13,000 dollars, for choosing the company BelAVM as an equipment supplier. The bribes were allegedly paid in October and November 2016 through intermediaries. The source reports arrests only, with no charges beyond that or a verdict.
cases.source_title: В Белоруссии раскрыли коррупционную сеть, созданную поставщиками компьютерной техники (MK)

cases.people: Abdelwahab Keramane (former governor)
cases.summary: In the Khalifa Bank case, the Blida criminal court sentenced former governor Abdelwahab Keramane in absentia to 20 years in prison in 2007. On 7 June 2022 the Blida criminal court acquitted him. The pages opened do not state the specific charges.
cases.source_title: Abdelmoumene Khalifa condamné à 18 ans de prison, huit autres accusés acquittés (Algérie Eco)

cases.people: Mohammad Al Hashel (governor)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: the Kuwaiti newspaper Al Jarida, citing unnamed sources, reported that the securities regulator had decided to refer Governor Mohammad Al Hashel to prosecutors for suspected breach of investment rules over shares in a local bank. He denied it, saying he had never traded shares in a listed company during his senior posts and that buying 2,172 shares in a capital increase did not use inside information. The regulator did not answer Reuters' calls and the article reports no outcome.
cases.source_title: Kuwait central bank chief denies illicit share trading (Gulf News)

cases.people: two convicted persons (unnamed in source)
cases.summary: The Misrata Criminal Court convicted two people of belonging to an organization set up to seize US$128 million and €5 million from the central bank's Sirte branch in 2013 through coercion. One got 15 years in prison and a LD 2.5 million fine; the other got 13 years and a LD 50,000 fine. The Attorney General's Office reported the ruling in October 2023.
cases.source_title: Two convicted for stealing Central Bank of Libya funds worth over US$ 128 million (Libya Herald)

cases.people: Saddek Elkaber (governor)
cases.summary: Global Witness reported that most Libyan letters of credit enter the international system through ABC International Bank in London, a commercial bank indirectly owned by the central bank and chaired by Governor Saddek Elkaber. It called this a clear conflict of interest, given his authority over letters of credit and anti-money-laundering rules. It built a database of nearly $2.5bn of letters of credit over 13 weeks in 2020 and said sources described mispricing, laundering and procurement fraud; the page reports no official finding of fraud.
cases.source_title: Global Witness reveals fraudulent Libyan Letters of Credit money entering international financial system via London (Global Witness)

cases.people: Ali al-Hibri (deputy governor); Saddek Elkaber (governor, complainant)
cases.summary: In November 2022 the central bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar banknotes it said were printed in Russia and bore his signature, and Governor Saddek Elkaber asked the Attorney-General to pursue a complaint. The bank did not say how many notes were involved. The article gives no response from al-Hibri and no later outcome.
cases.source_title: CBL governor files legal complaint against his deputy over forged banknotes (Libya Update)

cases.people: staff (none named or mentioned in source)
cases.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib said on 4 July 2019 that 1.2 million dirhams ($125,000) was stolen during a movement of cash from the Dar As-Sikkah mint to cities in northern Morocco. The bank called it an isolated but malicious act and opened an investigation; the page reports no findings or arrests.
cases.source_title: Moroccan central bank opens investigation into stolen cash (Central Banking)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib filed a complaint with the prosecutor's office against one of its staff and a service provider over suspected corruption in awarding contracts, after an internal investigation under its anti-corruption system. The article gives no amounts and no charges or ruling.
cases.source_title: BAM porte plainte contre un agent et un prestataire pour soupçons de corruption (Hespress)

cases.people: bank employee and others (names left out; pretrial suspects, no verdict found)
cases.summary: In July 2020 police under the Nouakchott-Ouest prosecutor arrested six people, including one bank employee, over foreign currency taken from the central bank; early reports said about $1 million and later reports $2.4 million, plus $500,000 in counterfeit notes. By March 2021 seven people were in pretrial detention, presumed to have taken about $1 million, and supporters held a sit-in demanding a quick trial. The pages opened report no trial or verdict.
cases.source_title: Mauritanie: six présumés voleurs du million de dollars à la Banque centrale arrêtés (Le360 Afrique)

cases.central_bank: Banque de la République du Burundi
cases.people: Dieudonné Murengerantwari (governor)
cases.summary: In October 2023 the Ministry of Justice said dismissed governor Dieudonné Murengerantwari was being prosecuted for passive corruption, money laundering, misappropriation of public property and undermining the national economy. The prosecutor called this description of the facts provisional, and he was being questioned at the time of the report.
cases.source_title: Burundi: Central Bank governor prosecuted for corruption (Africanews)

cases.people: Deogratias Mutombo (governor, 2013-2021)
cases.summary: An April 2021 report by Congo's IGF finance inspectorate called a 43 million USD transfer from a central bank account at BGFI Bank to food importer Egal an embezzlement of public funds, and said the bank kept false accounts to cover it. The bank's 2013 accounts showed about 43.1 million USD in that account when the real balance was about 119,000 USD. Mutombo, the bank and PwC did not respond to the journalists who reported this from leaked BGFI documents.
cases.source_title: Congo Hold-up : la caisse noire de la Banque centrale du Congo (Seneweb)

cases.people: Deogratias Mutombo (former governor)
cases.summary: Belgium's federal prosecutor opened a money laundering investigation into former governor Deogratias Mutombo and five others over hundreds of thousands of dollars allegedly moved through Belgium from DR Congo, with searches in September 2023. As of October 2024 the prosecutor said no suspect had been charged.
cases.source_title: Soupçons de blanchiment : la justice belge enquête sur l'ex-patron de la Banque centrale du Congo (Orishas Finance)

cases.people: Amadou Colley (governor)
cases.summary: The Janneh Commission found that governor Amadou Colley let former President Jammeh and General Sulayman Badjie withdraw funds without proper authorization, including millions of dollars by Badjie. A government White Paper banned Colley from public office for life and held him jointly liable for the money withdrawn in breach of the bank's procedures.
cases.source_title: Former CBG Governor Amadou Colley Banned From Holding Public Office For Life (Africa-Press)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: In March 2008 Ethiopian anti-corruption officials arrested 26 people after 90 kilos of fake gold were found in the central bank's vaults. Seven of those held were from the National Bank of Ethiopia, four from the Ethiopian Geological Survey and 15 were businessmen and collaborators. The report covers arrests only, not charges or court outcomes.
cases.source_title: Ethiopia makes arrests over fake gold scandal (Central Banking)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: The National Bank of Rwanda lost Rwf63 million from deposit accounts in early 2014 in a fraud reported to involve bank staff. The bank's ICT director said the suspects manipulated its internal security system before taking the cash. One person was arrested and the file sent to the Prosecutor General, while police said the prime suspect was believed to have fled to Uganda.
cases.source_title: Workers defraud central bank of Rwf63m, prime suspect on the run (The New Times)

cases.people: Bank of Zambia section officer (named in the source)
cases.summary: In October 2015 Zambia's Drug Enforcement Commission arrested Bank of Zambia a section officer for theft by a public servant and money laundering. He was accused of taking USD 43,660 and K20,335 in cash from his employer between January and September 2015. The report gives no court outcome.
cases.source_title: DEC arrests money laundering BoZ employee (QFM Zambia)

cases.people: Ernesto Gove (governor); Silvia de Abreu (board member)
cases.summary: Letters from 2013 presented in a US trial showed the Bank of Mozambique authorized Proindicus to seek a $372 million Credit Suisse loan, later $622 million, and Ematum an $850 million loan, part of the 'hidden debts' of over $2 billion. The letters were signed by board member Silvia de Abreu after a dispatch from governor Ernesto Gove, who in 2016 denied responsibility and said he had never heard of Proindicus. The newssheet Carta de Moçambique reported Gove's suspect status was confirmed and that he may face charges of abuse of office and membership of a criminal organisation.
cases.source_title: Bank of Mozambique involved in hidden debts – AIM report (Club of Mozambique)

cases.people: Ernesto Gove (former governor); board members (unnamed)
cases.summary: In April 2023 the daily Noticias, citing judicial sources, reported that former governor Ernesto Gove and two other central bank board members were among four accused in a second hidden debts trial being prepared. No trial date had been set, and the report lists no specific charges. Follow-up to the earlier record on the same case; no later outcome was confirmed in this search.
cases.source_title: Hidden debts: second trial under preparation (Club of Mozambique)

cases.people: former Deputy Governor (unnamed in source)
cases.summary: Final findings of Bhutan's Anti-Corruption Commission said a former Deputy Governor of the Royal Monetary Authority allegedly forged official documents, misused power and concealed earnings from World Bank and Asian Development Bank projects. An anonymous informer raised the case in October 2014. The case was forwarded to the Office of the Attorney General; the report gives no later outcome.
cases.source_title: RMA's former Deputy Governor allegedly forged official documents and misused power, says ACC findings (BBS)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: A former currency-exchange employee at the Bank of Korea's Daejeon Sejong-Chungnam headquarters broke the first-in, first-out rule at a coin collector's request, letting 240,000 100-won coins from 2018-2019 be issued before 2017 coins. The collector earned about 180 million won selling the coins and gave the employee about 55 million won. The Daejeon District Court sentenced the employee to 2 years 6 months in prison, a 1 million won fine and confiscation of about 43.31 million won.
cases.source_title: "Rare Coins Are Valuable"... Former Bank of Korea Employee Sentenced for Embezzling Coins (Asia Economy)

cases.people: news media staff (unnamed), not Reserve Bank staff
cases.summary: Information on the March Official Cash Rate cut was shared from the bank's media lock-up on 10 March and passed to an economics blogger before the official release. An independent investigation by Deloitte's forensic unit traced the leak to a Newshub Mediaworks reporter. The Reserve Bank ended embargoed lock-ups for news media and analysts.
cases.source_title: Reserve Bank takes action after investigation confirms leak (Reserve Bank of New Zealand)

cases.people: Rerngchai Marakanond (former governor)
cases.summary: A case was brought in 2001 after former governor Rerngchai Marakanond, among other policy-makers, decided to use the central bank's reserves to defend the baht during the Asian financial crisis. On October 5, 2016 Thailand's Supreme Court upheld a lower court's ruling that he had not acted improperly, closing the 15-year case.
cases.source_title: Former Bank of Thailand governor cleared of Asian financial crisis charges (Central Banking)

cases.people: Senior Exchange Control Officer (named in the source)
cases.summary: A Senior Exchange Control Officer at the National Reserve Bank of Tonga forged a Government bond to support another person's New Zealand visa application and asked for $2,500 pa'anga. She pleaded guilty to forgery, knowingly dealing with forged documents and obtaining money by false pretenses, and her employment was terminated. On May 21, 2019 the Supreme Court of Tonga gave her a two-year sentence, fully suspended, and ordered $800 compensation.
cases.source_title: Former Reserve Bank officer gets suspended sentence for serious fraud (Matangi Tonga)

cases.people: board of directors (as a group)
cases.summary: Tonga's Anti-Corruption Commissioner sued the bank and its directors, alleging that a 2024 staff payment (for example $6,600 to each of 73 staff) was an unlawful bonus linked to record profit, a breach of trust and misfeasance in public office. The board had described it as a one-off anniversary payout. On 20 November 2025 the Court of Appeal dismissed the proceedings, finding no reasonable cause of action against the bank and that the claim against the directors also failed.
cases.source_title: National Reserve Bank of Tonga v Anti-Corruption Commissioner [2025] TOCA 25 (Court of Appeal of Tonga, PacLII)

cases.people: BSP bank examiner (named in the source)
cases.summary: After auditing the Rural Bank of Sapang Dalaga in late 2005, a BSP examiner took consultancy fees from the bank through a third-party firm, collecting P5,000 monthly for a total of P103,500. The court found he used false pretenses and threatened BSP sanctions. The Sandiganbayan denied his appeal and affirmed the guilty verdict, with six years and one month to seven years in prison and perpetual disqualification from public office.
cases.source_title: Sandiganbayan upholds conviction of ex-BSP examiner (BusinessWorld)

cases.people: Former officer, BSP Supervision and Examination Sector (named in the source)
cases.summary: A former officer of the BSP's Supervision and Examination Sector obtained a loan from the Rural Bank of Kiamba, Sarangani, Inc. in 2006. The Ombudsman cleared him in 2011 of liability under Section 27(d) in relation to Section 36 of Republic Act 7653. On a petition by the BSP, the Supreme Court reversed the Ombudsman and ordered the filing of criminal charges; the report does not say whether they have been filed.
cases.source_title: SC orders filing of charges vs former BSP exec (Manila Times)

cases.people: Manager, BSP Bacolod office (named in the source)
cases.summary: BSP's internal audit reviewed cash at the Bacolod City branch, spotted thinner-than-standard bundles of P500 bills and found a shortfall of P5.955 million. In an affidavit, the branch manager reportedly said he used the money for lending and "treasure hunting". The Ombudsman found him guilty of dishonesty, ordered his dismissal with forfeiture of benefits, and was set to file malversation charges.
cases.source_title: Ombudsman orders dismissal of BSP exec (Philippine Star)

cases.people: staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: A BSP legal department investigation that began in November 2023 found four staff had falsified attendance records; they were dismissed in July 2024. In August 2025 the Monetary Board approved the maximum administrative penalties for two supervisors found involved in falsifying those records, including dismissal, forfeiture of retirement benefits and perpetual disqualification from public office.
cases.source_title: BSP hammer drops on bosses in 'ghost employee' scandal (Manila Bulletin)

cases.people: Benjamin Diokno (BSP Governor); six other BSP officials
cases.summary: In January 2021 the chairman of Stop Corruption Organization of the Philippines filed a graft complaint at the Ombudsman against Governor Benjamin Diokno and six other BSP officials over a P1.75-billion national ID card contract awarded to AllCard International. He alleged the bidding terms required buying materials from OVD Kinegram AG without separate public bidding. These are the complainant's allegations; the report gives no finding.
cases.source_title: Diokno, 6 other BSP execs sued over national ID deal (Philippine Star)

cases.people: Amando Tetangco Jr. (former BSP governor and Monetary Board chairman); Monetary Board members
cases.summary: A 2013 graft complaint at the Ombudsman, filed by Joselito Yujuico and others tied to GenBank, says former governor Amando Tetangco Jr., Monetary Board members and other officials caused undue injury and gave undue advantage to Allied Bank by allowing its merger with Philippine National Bank on February 9, 2013. In September 2025 the complaint was reported still pending, and the complainants asked for an immediate resolution.
cases.source_title: Ombudsman urged to resolve graft raps vs former BSP-MB execs (Malaya)

cases.people: Joseph Yam Chi-kwong (former HKMA chief)
cases.summary: A Legislative Council subcommittee report said former HKMA chief Joseph Yam Chi-kwong should bear "ultimate responsibility" for investors' losses from irregularities in Lehman's minibonds and structured products, because he headed the banking watchdog at the time. The HKMA replied that the report had not fully taken into account the information it submitted, and some members prepared a minority report.
cases.source_title: Lehman criticism played down (South China Morning Post)
cases.update_title: HKMA statement on the subcommittee report, 6 June 2012 (HKMA)

cases.people: Samson Ngwele (Governor)
cases.summary: A 3 July 1996 Ombudsman report found that Governor Samson Ngwele improperly executed ten bank guarantees totalling US$100,000,000, without Board approval and under pressure from Finance Minister Barak Sope, breaching the Reserve Bank Act and the Leadership Code. The guarantees went to Peter Harold Swanson for a 'Trading Programme' that the Ombudsman called a scam, and were still in circulation at the time of the report. The report commended the Governor's later attempts to remedy the situation; he disagreed with its adverse comments about him.
cases.source_title: The Provision of Bank Guarantees Given in the Sum of US$100,000,000.00 (Office of the Ombudsman, Vanuatu, via PacLII)

cases.people: Ahmed Naseer (Governor)
cases.summary: Governor Ahmed Naseer resigned in July 2019 amid allegations of circumventing the bank's regulations, after being summoned twice by parliament's public finance committee. Former Financial Intelligence Unit head Abdulla Ashraf alleged that Naseer interfered in unit investigations, including one into an MVR 22.5 million deposit to then-President Abdulla Yameen's account shortly before the 2018 election. Naseer denied trying to influence the unit and made counter-allegations against Ashraf; the article reports no charges or findings.
cases.source_title: The Edition report on Governor Ahmed Naseer's resignation, 24 July 2019 (The Edition)

cases.people: Thor Peng Leath (Governor); chief of the supervision department (unnamed here)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: the Phnom Penh Post reported that Governor Thor Peng Leath issued a $3 million central bank loan on 31 May 1994 so Credit Bank of Cambodia could meet minimum capital requirements, which central bank officials admitted was 'highly irregular', and that on 8 May 1995 the bank let $145,000 be withdrawn from former commerce minister Var Huot's account after the bank's assets were frozen. Creditors and senior officials claimed preferential treatment; Var Huot said there was none. The article reports no charges or findings against central bank officials.
cases.source_title: National Bank tangled in CBC money scandal (Phnom Penh Post)

cases.people: Jacob Frenkel (former Governor); senior bank official (unnamed)
cases.summary: State Comptroller Eliezer Goldberg's report, published 29 April 2002, said former governor Jacob Frenkel unlawfully received hundreds of thousands of shekels when he resigned. It said he demanded and received refunds and payments his predecessors did not get, approved by a senior bank official who reported to him. Goldberg did not say whether the state should demand the money back.
cases.source_title: Comptroller: Frenkel received unlawful compensation from Bank of Israel (Globes)

cases.people: Banking Supervision Department staff (unnamed); Rony Hizkiyahu (Supervisor of Banks, recipient of the draft)
cases.summary: Globes reported on 3 February 2009, citing sources, that a draft report by State Comptroller Micha Lindenstrauss found alleged flaws in how the bank's supervision department handled sub-prime investments at Bank Hapoalim, which had written off $1.5 billion on them, and that the bank had only partial information about Israeli banks' exposure to risky instruments. This was a draft: the bank was preparing its reply and said it had responses to all the points.
cases.source_title: Regulator faulted on Hapoalim sub-prime investments (Globes)

cases.people: Derick Latibeaudiere (governor)
cases.summary: Governor Derick Latibeaudiere borrowed $51 million from the central bank for a house, furnishings and landscaping. At a Public Accounts Committee hearing on 26 May 2009, Auditor General Pamela Monroe Ellis said she had no documents showing the loans were secured and that a $25 million part was still unsecured. The bank's lawyer said $30 million was fully secured against the governor's house, and the committee told both sides to resolve their differences and report back.
cases.source_title: After nine months ... Still no proof of collateral from Bank of Jamaica (Jamaica Gleaner)

cases.central_bank: Banca Centrale della Repubblica di San Marino
cases.people: Catia Tomasetti (president)
cases.summary: Investigators suspected a 220,000 euro payment from the central bank to Sandro Gozi for a consultancy they considered fictitious, in a case against Gozi and bank president Catia Tomasetti that became public in April 2019. The Tribunal of San Marino dismissed the case in 2020, finding no relevant conduct by either suspect. The article reports that the consultancy was real.
cases.source_title: L'archiviazione silenziosa di Sandro Gozi (Il Foglio)

cases.people: Tom Alweendo (governor)
cases.summary: Court papers in a suit brought by Nambib Resources against the Minister of Mines listed governor Tom Alweendo as a 10 per cent shareholder in Trade Line Namibia, which had been given an exclusive prospecting licence on the Skeleton Coast. Alweendo said he was made a director of the company without his knowledge. The article reports no finding or outcome.
cases.source_title: Namibian c bank chief 'was not aware of gem link' (Central Banking)

cases.people: Lesotho officials (unnamed; the source does not say whether any worked at the central bank)
cases.summary: In February 2024 three South Africans appeared in the Ficksburg Magistrates Court on fraud and money laundering charges over R57 million allegedly stolen from the Central Bank of Lesotho. The Hawks said Lesotho officials intercepted vouchers meant for service providers and diverted the payments to co-conspirators in South Africa, and that some officials were already before court in Lesotho.
cases.source_title: South Africans nabbed for stealing from Central Bank of Lesotho appear in court (EWN)

cases.people: none named at the central bank
cases.summary: On 20 July 2021 Fernando Anastácio, rapporteur of the parliamentary inquiry into Novo Banco's losses, presented a proposed final report saying supervision failed across the board and that there was a permanent and systematic failure. This was a draft, and the PSD said its deputies would vote against it and propose amendments.
cases.source_title: Supervisão do Banco de Portugal falhou em toda a linha nos problemas do Novo Banco (Observador)

cases.people: Head of a division in NBP's IT and Telecommunications Department
cases.summary: In February 2009 Poland's Central Anti-Corruption Bureau said its officers detained eight people in a case against a division head in the NBP's IT and telecommunications department. He was accused of taking bribes worth at least 350,000 zloty to rig tenders between 2001 and 2008, and prosecutors charged the businessmen who ran an IT systems firm with giving him bribes.
cases.source_title: Naczelnik z NBP zamieszany w korupcyjny proceder (Centralne Biuro Antykorupcyjne)

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of the Islamic Republic of Iran
cases.people: Three Future Bank officials (unnamed)
cases.summary: Asharq Al-Awsat reported in November 2020 that Bahrain's High Criminal Court fined the Central Bank of Iran and other Iran-owned banks, including Future Bank, BD 1 million each, and jailed three Future Bank officials for five years. Prosecutors said the Central Bank of Iran planned to launder billions of dollars through Future Bank, which handled suspicious SWIFT transfers favoring Iranian entities, mainly the central bank, without reporting them.
cases.source_title: Bahraini Court Fines Central Bank of Iran in Money Laundering Case (Asharq Al-Awsat)

cases.people: Laurent Gbagbo (former president); Gilbert Aké N'Gbo (former prime minister); Koné Katinan (former budget minister); Désiré Dallo (former economy and finance minister)
cases.summary: On 18 January 2018 a court in Côte d'Ivoire, with judge Sombé Méïté giving the verdict, sentenced Gbagbo, Aké N'Gbo, Katinan and Dallo to 20 years in prison and a 329 billion CFA franc fine for offences including group theft by break-in of BCEAO vaults and cash during the December 2010 to April 2011 post-election crisis. Seven bailiffs got 36 months and a 700,000 CFA franc fine. Katinan was absent throughout the trial. Gbagbo always denied the charges, and on 6 August 2022 President Ouattara pardoned him.
cases.source_title: Braquage BCEAO: Gbagbo et 3 de ses ex-ministres condamnés à 20 ans de prison et 329 milliards FCFA d'amende (Abidjan.net, citing APA)
cases.update_title: Ivory Coast president pardons predecessor, Laurent Gbagbo (Al Jazeera, 2022)

cases.country: Côte d'Ivoire (BCEAO, regional central bank of UEMOA)
cases.central_bank: Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest
cases.people: Philippe-Henri Dacoury-Tabley (governor)
cases.summary: A summit of UEMOA heads of state accepted governor Dacoury-Tabley's resignation in January 2011. He was criticized for ignoring a 23 December decision by UEMOA finance ministers that gave Alassane Ouattara power over the institution, and the article says the BCEAO paid out 60 to 100 billion CFA francs to the Gbagbo regime after that date. Senegal's President Abdoulaye Wade asked for an audit and alleged that the former governor moved 500 billion CFA francs to Gbagbo after being dismissed; another figure cited is 300 billion, and that report gives no audit result.
cases.source_title: BCEAO: démission du gouverneur Dacoury, un proche de l'ancien président Gbagbo (Connectionivoirienne, with Nettali.net)
cases.update_title: Bceao : Au-delà de l'audit de Wade (Abidjan.net, Le Journal de l'Economie)

cases.people: Accused businesswoman (named in the source); Ian Khama (former president); Isaac Kgosi (former intelligence service head)
cases.summary: A woman arrested on 17 October 2019 was implicated with others including former president Ian Khama and former intelligence head Isaac Kgosi in allegedly stealing P100 billion from Bank of Botswana. High Court Judge Zein Kebonang discharged and acquitted her of unexplained property and a false passport declaration, the state withdrew a terrorism financing charge, and he found the accusations fabricated. He referred the investigator to police for perjury prosecution.
cases.source_title: Butterfly walks free (The Patriot on Sunday)

cases.people: Kelfala Morana Kallon (governor)
cases.summary: Governor Kallon told Parliament on 22 November 2021 that he "bribed" people hoarding the Leone to bring it back into the banking system. The Anti-Corruption Commission investigated and said in May 2022 that he was referring to cash swap operations in which the bank sold about US$68.6 million in foreign currency in 2021, that the word was used in error, and that it had closed the investigation after advising him to choose his words more carefully.
cases.source_title: ACC concludes investigation of "bribe" statement by the governor of bank of Sierra Leone (Sierra Leone Telegraph)

cases.central_bank: Banco Central de la República Argentina
cases.people: BCRA officials (unnamed)
cases.summary: La Nación reported on 17 April 2026 that the BCRA is examining a circuit that moved at least US$900 million between January 2022 and October 2023, in which dollars bought at the official rate allegedly ended up in the parallel market through exchange houses. The BCRA opened procedures against officials over its ethics rules, after raids at the bank that followed reports from the UIF and Procelac. The companies deny wrongdoing.
cases.source_title: El Banco Central investiga operaciones irregulares por US$900 millones durante el último gobierno (La Nación)

cases.central_bank: Banco Central de Sao Tome e Principe
cases.people: Maria do Carmo Silveira (central bank governor, former prime minister)
cases.summary: In June 2006 Sao Tome's cabinet dismissed central bank governor Maria do Carmo Silveira and her team, saying it had found irregularities in the construction of the new central bank building, a project valued at US$8 million. The report gives no detail on the irregularities and no investigation finding.
cases.source_title: Sao Tome government fires central bank governor (Central Banking)

cases.people: Ahmed Naseer (governor, Maldives Monetary Authority)
cases.summary: In March 2019 police summoned Maldives Monetary Authority governor Ahmed Naseer and confirmed he was being investigated for obstruction of justice. Parliament's Financial Committee had questioned him on 5 March about the Anti-Corruption Commission report on the embezzlement case at the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation and about the removal of Abdulla Ashraf as head of the Financial Intelligence Unit. The report names no charge or court outcome.
cases.source_title: Governor of Maldives Monetary Authority summoned by police (Edition.mv)

cases.people: Carlos Costa (governor); Elisa Ferreira (vice-governor); Jose da Cunha Pereira (ethics committee member)
cases.summary: The Banco de Portugal's ethics committee examined a request by governor Carlos Costa to be excused from matters concerning Caixa Geral de Depositos, discussed at a meeting in April 2019 after an EY audit of CGD's management. Costa had been a CGD board member from 2004 to 2006 and may have sat on extended credit council meetings that approved operations which caused losses, while now heading the supervisor assessing former CGD directors. Vice-governor Elisa Ferreira did not recuse herself but told the committee of a possible conflict of interest relating to her husband's past role at La Seda. The committee's conclusions were not made public. No conclusion was published.
cases.source_title: Comissao de etica do Banco de Portugal analisou escusa do governador na Caixa (Observador)

cases.people: Central Bank of Iran (as a convicted party); six unnamed Future Bank officials; Wael Bualai (Bahrain attorney general)
cases.summary: Each convicted party, including the Central Bank of Iran, was fined one million Bahraini dinars; five Future Bank officials received 10-year prison sentences and a sixth five years. The court upheld confiscation of remittances estimated at $184 million, 967 million euros, 53 million dirhams and 235 billion Iranian riyals. The report was updated 2 November 2021.
cases.source_title: Bahrain top court upholds money laundering conviction against Central Bank of Iran (Gulf News)

cases.category: prosecution over central bank investment deal
cases.people: Siim Kallas (former president of the Bank of Estonia, Reform Party leader); Jaan Naaber (prosecutor)
cases.summary: Naaber asked a district court to convict Kallas and an unnamed co-defendant over their role in the deal.
cases.source_title: Appeal filed in Kallas case (The Baltic Times)

cases.people: Ibrahim Athif Shakoor (former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit at the Maldives Monetary Authority); Azeema Adam (MMA governor at the time, named by Shakoor)
cases.summary: In February 2020 the Prosecutor General's Office charged Ibrahim Athif Shakoor, former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit at the Maldives Monetary Authority, with negligence and failing to act appropriately on the MMPRC case, in which state funds were moved to private accounts. At a preliminary hearing at the Criminal Court in September 2020 he asked the Prosecutor General's Office to arrange a confessional agreement waiving prison in exchange for admitting a breach of the money laundering and terrorism financing law. He said he had told the then MMA governor, Azeema Adam, about illegal MMPRC transactions at least four times and had also tried to alert police; he denied the allegations at an August 2019 Public Finance Committee meeting. Atoll Times reported on 14 October 2025 that the Prosecutor General’s Office withdrew the charge, saying it qualified for an advisory agreement and citing how long the case had been in court. No conviction is reported.
cases.source_title: Athif seeks confessional agreement in MMPRC-linked case (Edition.mv)
cases.update_title: Charges withdrawn against Athif over MMPRC graft scandal (Atoll Times)

cases.central_bank: Banco Central de la Republica Dominicana
cases.category: missing bank assets / breach of trust charges
cases.people: Jose Lois Malkun (former governor); Felix Calvo (former deputy governor); Cesar Apolinar Veloz (former administrative director); Manuel Rubio Cristoforis (former legal counsel); Manuel Arturo Pellerano (former banker); Olga Morel (central bank legal counsel)
cases.summary: The Direccion de Persecucion de la Corrupcion Administrativa brought former Banco Central governor Jose Lois Malkun, former deputy governor Felix Calvo, former administrative director Cesar Apolinar Veloz and former legal counsel Manuel Rubio Cristoforis to court on charges including breach of trust (abuso de confianza) and criminal association, over the disappearance of 18 promissory notes worth RD$10,663 million said to have been handed fraudulently to former banker Manuel Arturo Pellerano. The Banco Central neither filed a complaint nor joined as a civil party; a Junta Monetaria resolution signed by legal counsel Olga Morel said the bank's authorities were negotiating the return of the notes with Pellerano.
cases.source_title: Bancentral no se querella contra tres ex funcionarios (El Dia)

cases.people: Farijala Hussein and Rajabu Maranda (businessmen)
cases.summary: The Kisutu Resident Magistrate's Court in Dar es Salaam sentenced businessmen Farijala Hussein and Rajabu Maranda to five years in prison, finding them guilty of offences related to financial impropriety, forgery and obtaining credit under false pretences, and ordered them to return the money they had taken. The report, published 27 May 2011, describes these as the first court cases heard after the 2008 Bank of Tanzania corruption scandal. No amount is given.
cases.source_title: Tanzania jails two over central bank corruption scandal (Central Banking)

cases.central_bank: Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago
cases.category: supervisory failure found by a commission of enquiry
cases.people: Sir Anthony Colman (sole commissioner); the Inspector of financial institutions (unnamed); Lawrence Duprey (CL Financial chairman); Harry Harnarine (Hindu Credit Union chairman)
cases.summary: The commission of enquiry into the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union, run by sole commissioner Sir Anthony Colman and commissioned in November 2010, found the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's powers of regulatory control over the insurance industry to be 'fundamentally deficient', tracing this to the Insurance Act's inadequate regulatory scope. The report said the Inspector of financial institutions tried to use the limited tools then available but that Clico and CL Financial management largely ignored them, and that had some powers in an unenacted Insurance Bill been in force by 2008 the collapse might have been avoided. It blamed no named Central Bank official. The enquiry sat from March 2011 to May 2013 at an estimated cost of $36.2 million, including a $7 million fee for Colman.
cases.source_title: Colman report knocks T&T Central Bank in Clico, HCU fiasco (Stabroek News)

cases.category: licensing decision overridden by political pressure
cases.people: Majozi Sithole (governor); Martin Dlamini (finance minister); Manqoba Khumalo (minister of commerce, industry and trade)
cases.summary: The Central Bank of Eswatini rejected Farmers Bank's commercial banking licence application in late 2017, then granted it after a royal command in September 2018. Governor Majozi Sithole said he was given a royal command to attend a 14 July 2017 meeting about the bank, and in May 2018 finance minister Martin Dlamini told the central bank the king had ordered an investigation into its reluctance to license it. The central bank revoked the licence on 5 October 2020 over the unexplained source of the seed capital, commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo ruled in December 2020 that the bank should keep it, and the central bank reinstated it in January 2021 while objecting to procedural improprieties.
cases.source_title: The central bank in a tiny African country tried to block a suspicious banking venture. Then the king's allies intervened. (ICIJ, Swazi Secrets)

cases.category: conflict of interest at the monetary authority
cases.people: George McCarthy (board chairman); Cindy Scotland (managing director); Gloria Glidden (deputy head of the banking division)
cases.summary: In June 2015 the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority said it would commission an internal review of the involvement of local people and financial institutions in the FIFA corruption case, after Caymanian businessman Jeffrey Webb was arrested in Switzerland on 27 May. Managing director Cindy Scotland's husband, former minister Mark Scotland, had worked for the Cayman Islands Football Association under Webb and was with Webb at the arrest, and Gloria Glidden, deputy head of the authority's banking division, is the wife of former minister Cline Glidden, who was also in Switzerland with Webb. Chairman George McCarthy said Scotland would remain managing director and that there was no evidence any Cayman bank had done anything wrong.
cases.source_title: Cayman's financial regulator begins internal review (Cayman Compass)

cases.category: loss of bank funds to payment fraud; dismissal disputed
cases.people: Former head of the bank's accounting management department (Departamento de Gestion Contable), not named here; Rossana Costa (bank president, summoned as witness); Beltran Ramon (general manager, summoned)
cases.summary: In March 2022 someone posing as the chief financial officer of the US firm RVK emailed the Banco Central de Chile a false invoice for US$205,000 from an address differing from the real one by one letter, then asked for payment to a new account at another bank, and the bank paid. The bank filed a complaint with the Ministerio Publico in May 2022 and dismissed the head of its accounting management department on 23 June 2022 as an administrative sanction for the erroneous payment; he sued in the First Labour Court of Santiago in December, calling the dismissal abusive and unfair and seeking 267 million pesos. The bank said there was no indication that any official took part deliberately.
cases.source_title: Banco Central demandado por 267 millones por despido en caso de suplantacion y fraude (Meganoticias)
cases.update_title: Banco Central inicia investigacion por pago de 170 millones a cuenta de suplantador (BioBioChile)

cases.category: diversion of funds from banks the central bank had intervened in; conviction of the central bank's banking superintendent
cases.people: Jose Pecci (former superintendent of the institute emisor, sentenced to eight years); Luis Gonzalez Macchi (President of Paraguay 1999-2003)
cases.summary: On 6 June 2006 a sentencing court in Asuncion presided by Sandra Farias, with Gustavo Amarilla and Miguel Said, sentenced former president Luis Gonzalez Macchi to six years in prison for lesion de confianza as alleged instigator of the diversion of US$16 million to the United States from two private banks, Union and Orienta, which the Banco Central intervened in and declared bankrupt. The report states that Jose Pecci, former superintendent of the institute emisor, was sentenced to eight years, without explaining his role. Gonzalez Macchi said he would appeal; prosecutor Victoria Acuna had sought ten years. An appeals court later cleared Gonzalez Macchi, saying the evidence was insufficient; that ruling is recorded separately here.
cases.source_title: Condenan a seis anos de carcel al ex presidente de Paraguay (Notife)
cases.update_title: Central Banking article on the impeachment of President Gonzalez Macchi, 29 January 2003 (Central Banking)

cases.category: supervisory failure found by anti-corruption body
cases.people: Azeema Adam (former governor); Ibrahim Athif Shakoor (former head of the Financial Intelligence Unit)
cases.summary: An Anti-Corruption Commission report publicised in February 2019 found the Maldives Monetary Authority negligent in the MMPRC case, in which MVR 1.3 billion was embezzled from Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation. The commission found the authority's Financial Intelligence Unit was told in 2014 of a US$59 million cheque from MMPRC to the company SOF but did not investigate it properly, did not examine large SOF transactions through Bank of Maldives and Bank of Ceylon, and did not forward suspected money-laundering cases to the relevant authorities. Former FIU head Ibrahim Athif Shakoor said governor Azeema Adam objected to filing a police report, citing insufficient FIU staff and resources; Azeema said she had told the FIU head to investigate SOF's transactions and gave no specific instructions because the FIU decided its own actions.
cases.source_title: ACC finds MMA negligent in MMPRC scandal (Edition.mv)

cases.category: central bank authorisation of state-guaranteed loans
cases.people: Ernesto Gove (former governor, testifying as a witness)
cases.summary: Testifying as a witness at the Maputo City Court on 23 November 2021 in the hidden debts trial of 19 people, former Bank of Mozambique governor Ernesto Gove said he signed authorisations for foreign loans to Proindicus, Ematum and MAM on grounds of sovereignty and national security, and admitted irregularities in how the central bank granted them, including that the requests were handed personally to senior bank officials by Eugenio Matlaba and Antonio Carlos do Rosario rather than submitted at a counter, and that the financing contracts with Credit Suisse had already been signed. Article 83 of the Foreign Exchange Law regulations bars the central bank from authorising foreign loans to private companies whose repayment depends on a state guarantee; Gove argued it applied only to guarantees obtained after loans were agreed, and judge Efigenio Baptista rejected that reading. The loans exceeded two billion US dollars, from Credit Suisse and VTB of Russia.
cases.source_title: Hidden debts trial: Illegal loans were in interests of 'sovereignty', claims ex-governor of Bank of Mozambique (Club of Mozambique / AIM)

cases.category: conflict of interest in a senior appointment
cases.people: Nicolai Tangen (incoming CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management); Oystein Olsen (chair of the Norges Bank Executive Board); Julie Brodtkorb (chair of the Norges Bank Supervisory Board)
cases.summary: In August 2020 Norges Bank's Executive Board revised incoming NBIM chief executive Nicolai Tangen's employment terms to reduce conflict-of-interest concerns raised by the Storting's Standing Committee on Finance and Economic Affairs: Tangen would divest his holding in AKO Capital LLP and transfer his holding and dividend rights to the charitable AKO Foundation, with no ownership interest in AKO Capital in perpetuity, and would hold all his personal fund assets as bank deposits. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said there had been a breach of guidelines, regulations and laws in Tangen's appointment. Executive Board chair Oystein Olsen said the board had believed the existing contractual framework was sufficient but acknowledged the Storting took a different view. Tangen could take office on 1 September.
cases.source_title: NBIM revises Nicolai Tangen terms following conflict of interest concerns (European Pensions)

cases.category: unilateral change to sanctions enforcement procedure
cases.people: Natia Turnava (acting president of the National Bank of Georgia); Papuna Lezhava (vice-president and board member, resigned)
cases.summary: ADDS TURNAVA'S OWN ACCOUNT. At a briefing on 20 September 2023, acting National Bank of Georgia president Natia Turnava confirmed she had single-handedly adopted a change to the procedure for executing sanctions regimes, made on 19 September and effective 20 September 2023, saying it fell within the discretion of the bank's president and that she had informed National Bank Council members in advance. TBC Bank and Bank of Georgia had frozen the accounts of Otar Partskhaladze; Turnava said the banks did not violate the law because the amendment took effect the day of her briefing. Vice-president Papuna Lezhava resigned, for reasons the report says are unknown.
cases.source_title: Turnava confirms that she single-handedly changed the procedure for implementing the sanctions regimes (GBC)

cases.category: prosecution of central bank leadership over bank losses
cases.people: Grzegorz Wojtowicz (NBP president)
cases.summary: In the ArtB cheque-float affair, arrests after the owners of the company fled in summer 1991 included the president of Narodowy Bank Polski, Grzegorz Wojtowicz. He was charged with unintentionally causing bank losses of about 72 billion old zloty, and the court acquitted him. Prison sentences went to several employees of state banks, which the article does not identify as NBP staff.
cases.source_title: Afera ArtB. Najslynniejszy oscylator w krotkiej historii III RP (Forsal / Dziennik Gazeta Prawna)

cases.category: central bank approval of state-guaranteed loans (later development in the hidden-debts case)
cases.people: Silvina de Abreu (Banco de Mocambique administrator for monetary stability; director of the Foreign Exchange Department in 2013); Ernesto Gove (former governor); Waldemar de Sousa (administrator); Telma Goncalves (head of service); Antonio Carlos do Rosario (presented the EMATUM file); Manuel Chang (former finance minister)
cases.summary: On the 49th day of the trial, 23 November 2021, Banco de Mocambique administrator Silvina de Abreu testified that under normal conditions the central bank should not have authorised the ProIndicus, EMATUM and MAM loans, because the Foreign Exchange Law bars approving loans whose disbursement depends on a State guarantee. She said then governor Ernesto Gove told her to work only with the management group and not to involve technical staff, as the file concerned state security and sovereignty. The approvals she described were US$372 million for ProIndicus in March 2013, US$850 million for EMATUM in August 2013 and a further US$250 million sought for ProIndicus less than three months later.
cases.source_title: 49o dia do julgamento do escandalo das 'dividas ocultas': Banco de Mocambique nao deveria ter autorizado emprestimos da ProIndicus, EMATUM e MAM (CDD Mocambique trial-monitoring bulletin, Year 03 No. 255)

cases.people: former Bank of Korea employee, museum operations team (identified in the source only as 'A', aged 55)
cases.summary: A former Bank of Korea employee, moved in 2013 to the museum operations team and responsible for paying in the proceeds of Bank of Korea publication sales, diverted about 56 million won in 14 transfers to a personal account and used a Bank of Korea corporate card to buy about 12 million won of commemorative uncut banknote sheets. The Seoul Central District Court, Judge Lee Heung-kwon presiding, convicted the employee of occupational breach of trust and embezzlement and imposed eight months in prison suspended for two years, noting the full amount had been repaid.
cases.source_title: Naratdon ppaedollin jeon Haneun jigwon jiphaengyuye 2nyeon seongo (Saturday Economy / sateconomy.co.kr)

cases.category: attempt to try the governor before the State Tribunal (later development in an existing case)
cases.people: Adam Glapinski (governor of the National Bank of Poland)
cases.summary: On 20 August 2024 the Constitutional Tribunal, in a five-judge panel including chief justice Julia Przylebska, ruled that the legislation allowing him to be brought before the constitutional accountability committee is unconstitutional. The same court had ruled on 12 January 2024 that a three-fifths majority was required rather than a simple majority; the coalition held 241 of 460 seats against a threshold of 276.
cases.source_title: Poland's constitutional court rules parliament cannot put central bank chief on trial (Notes from Poland)

cases.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia
cases.people: Anita Angelovska Bezhoska (central bank governor, named on the page as 'Antia Bezoska')
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: an association of Eurostandard Bank depositors said in a press release that the central bank governor tipped off the finance minister and other large depositors so they could take their money out before the bank was put under administration, and that financial police reports were kept secret so the bank could keep operating. The association said Finance Minister Nina Angelovska withdrew more than 200,000 euros months before the central bank acted, and that over 60 million euros were lost. The page reports no charges and no official finding.
cases.source_title: Central bank governor was involved in the criminal activities surrounding the Eurostandard bank, depositors allege (Republika English)

cases.people: Adam Glapinski (president of Narodowy Bank Polski)
cases.summary: The motion, begun in May 2024, accuses Glapinski of indirectly financing the budget deficit through asset purchases in 2020-2021 and of acting without proper authorisation from the Monetary Policy Council for those purchases and for foreign-exchange interventions. Glapinski and the bank called the allegations baseless; no vote had taken place when the article was published.
cases.source_title: Sejm vote on referring NBP president Adam Glapinski to the State Tribunal planned for late November (XYZ.pl)

cases.category: cash handed out of the central bank on political instruction
cases.people: The Governor of the Central Bank of The Gambia and his deputies (named only by title in the document); General Sulayman (Saul) Badjie
cases.summary: The Gambian government's White Paper on the Commission of Inquiry into former president Yahya Jammeh's financial dealings accepted the finding that between September 2015 and January 2017 General Sulayman Badjie, purportedly acting for Jammeh, issued instructions to the Governor of the Central Bank or his deputies for withdrawals of US dollars, and that cash was handed over by the Governor to soldiers and loaded into vehicles. The Commission held Badjie accountable for illegal withdrawals of $15,785,601, 300,000 euros and D9,606,000, and the government ordered the money recovered through forfeiture and sale of his properties. The document also records $28.5 million illegally granted in the CBG 3M Account in 2000-2001 and $268,000 of money stolen from the Central Bank used to buy the Observer Newspaper.
cases.source_title: Government White Paper on the Report of the Commission of Inquiry into the financial dealings of former President Yahya Jammeh (Ministry of Justice, The Gambia)

cases.category: conflict of interest / paid outside directorship
cases.people: Saddek Elkaber (Governor of the Central Bank of Libya)
cases.summary: A Global Witness investigation published on 19 February 2021 found that senior Central Bank of Libya officials hold paid overseas directorships, and that Governor Saddek Elkaber chairs a London-based bank indirectly owned by the Central Bank of Libya, which the report calls a conflict of interest. The report also said the bank's letters of credit data point to ongoing financial crime in the system, citing nearly $2.5bn of private sector letters of credit approved between April and July 2020 and a $110m letter of credit for power equipment diverted to a UAE company with a near identical name to the original contractor. The report states it makes no allegation that any individual or bank broke the law.
cases.source_title: Discredited (Global Witness)

cases.category: misappropriation case against a former central bank head
cases.people: Humberto Capote (former president of the Banco Central del Uruguay)
cases.summary: Prosecutor Rodrigo Morosoli, investigating the Cambio Nelson fraud, sought the formal indictment of Humberto Capote, a former president of the Banco Central del Uruguay, for co-authorship of a continued crime of misappropriation. Judge Marcelo Souto freed Capote at first instance, finding the evidence insufficient to prosecute him, and the prosecutor appealed in April 2017.
cases.source_title: Fiscal apeló fallo del Cambio Nelson y pidió detención de ex titular del BCU (Montevideo Portal)

cases.category: criminal investigation of the central bank; seizure of ECB information
cases.people: Bank of Slovenia staff (unnamed)
cases.summary: Slovenian authorities searched the premises of Banka Slovenije on 6 July 2016 in a pre-criminal investigation procedure. The central bank published letters from the ECB President to Slovenia's State Prosecutor General, Mr Fiser, and to European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker about the seizure of ECB information during the search. This is a later step in the long-running inquiry into the 2013 Slovenian bank bailout.

cases.central_bank: National Bank of the Republic of Belarus
cases.category: bribes from IT suppliers to senior bank officials
cases.people: Feliks Kasperovich (held National Bank posts from 2005 to 2018; chairman of the board of the Belarusian Interbank Settlement Center); Andrei Podgorny (deputy head of the National Bank's Main Directorate of Information Technologies); Igor Kudasov (head of the National Bank's Main Directorate of Payment Systems and Digital Technologies)
cases.summary: At the trial reported in March 2020, prosecutors charged Feliks Kasperovich, together with Andrei Podgorny of the National Bank's information technology directorate, with taking bribes of at least $868,750, starting with $10,000 in 2007 and including $260,000 paid in 2016. Igor Kudasov, head of the bank's payment systems directorate, was charged with taking a $30,000 bribe and had been held in custody since 29 December 2018. Kasperovich admitted the charges in full. This is the trial stage of the computer-supply bribery network reported in 2016.
cases.source_title: Судят экс-начальника президентской охраны Втюрина и директора «Белтелекома» Сиводедова (Onliner)

cases.category: alleged embezzlement of central bank funds - later development: accounts frozen

cases.category: state audit finding: weak controls over reserves dealing and conflict-of-interest handling
cases.people: Bank of Israel Market Operations Division staff (unnamed); the Governor as chair of the foreign currency committee and the narrow monetary committee (not named in the source)
cases.summary: A State Comptroller's report, reported on 17 October 2012, found faults in how the Bank of Israel managed foreign currency reserves that had grown from USD 28 billion to USD 75 billion since March 2008. It said supervision and control of the Market Operations Division were deficient, there was no control over the receipt of bids, handling of possible employee conflicts of interest was incomplete, and the two committees chaired by the Governor worked without written procedures. The Bank said some issues were corrected during the audit and others were being addressed.
cases.source_title: State Comptroller report on Bank of Israel foreign currency reserves management (Globes)

cases.category: outside pressure on bank licensing; forensic report found third parties instructed the bank
cases.people: Central Bank of Eswatini evaluations team (unnamed); King Mswati III; Manqoba Khumalo (commerce minister, chaired the licence appeal)
cases.summary: In 2017 a Central Bank of Eswatini evaluations team recommended the board reject a commercial banking licence for Farmers Bank, warning it would tarnish the integrity of the bank's licensing policy, but a conditional licence was issued in September 2018 after a royal command from King Mswati III. The central bank revoked the licence in October 2020 because the bank could not prove the origin of its seed capital; an appeal chaired by commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo reinstated it in January 2021. A 2022 report by Kroll, commissioned by the central bank, said it was likely that third parties outside the bank intervened in the process and instructed it to proceed, and that R89m of seed capital had been used from 2019 to buy silver bullion the central bank could not verify existed.
cases.source_title: Swazi Secrets part 3: How to capture a bank (Financial Mail / amaBhungane and Finance Uncovered)

cases.category: conflicted appointments to the committee selecting the central bank's board
cases.people: Surapong Suebwonglee (former finance minister); Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi (appointed to the selection committee)
cases.summary: The Supreme Court's Criminal Division for Holders of Political Positions convicted former finance minister Surapong Suebwonglee of malfeasance under Section 157 of the Criminal Code for appointing Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi in 2008 to the committee that selects Bank of Thailand board members; the article says all three were representatives of financial institutions under Bank of Thailand supervision. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and a fine of 20,000 baht. The National Anti-Corruption Commission filed the case on 27 May 2015.
cases.source_title: Ex-finance minister gets suspended jail term (Bangkok Post)

cases.category: parliamentary inquiry into Novo Banco - later development: final report approved
cases.people: none named at the central bank; Fernando Negrão (chair of the inquiry committee)
cases.summary: Later development in the Novo Banco inquiry: on Tuesday 27 July 2021 Portugal's parliamentary committee of inquiry approved its final report, with the PS voting against and the CDS-PP abstaining. The report concludes that the resolution of BES and the initial capitalisation of Novo Banco, of 4,900 million euros, were a political fraud, and it leaves criticism of the Banco de Portugal and the European Commission. The article does not set out what those criticisms are, and names no Banco de Portugal officials.
cases.source_title: Aprovado relatório final da comissão de inquérito ao Novo Banco (Dinheiro Vivo)

cases.category: alleged supervisory failure over CLICO (claim made at a commission of enquiry)
cases.people: Ewart Williams (governor, cross-examined as a witness); Peter Carter QC (counsel at the enquiry)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: at the Commission of Enquiry into the collapse of CL Financial and the Hindu Credit Union, Queen's Counsel Peter Carter put it to former Central Bank governor Ewart Williams on 6 December 2012 that if the Central Bank had intervened in 2006, over TT$10 billion would not have been at risk. Williams had said the bank saw early warning signs at CLICO in 2006 but held off to avoid a run on the insurer; the Central Bank intervened in 2009. This was cross-examination of a witness, not a finding by the commission.
cases.source_title: QC: T&T Central Bank could have protected CLICO TT$10b (Stabroek News)

cases.category: nepotism and conflict of interest in a senior appointment (criticism, not a finding)
cases.people: Chea Serey (promoted to director-general); Chea Chanto (governor, her father); Tioulong Saumura (former NBC deputy governor, critic)
cases.summary: Claim, not confirmed: the Cambodia Daily reported on 28 November 2013 that Chea Serey, daughter of National Bank of Cambodia governor Chea Chanto, was promoted from deputy director-general for banking supervision to director-general, replacing Nguon Sokha. Tioulong Saumura, a former NBC deputy governor, said the fact that she is the governor's daughter should exclude her, citing nepotism and conflict of interest; Nguon Sokha said Serey is a skilled technocrat fit to run the central bank. No investigation or finding is reported.
cases.source_title: Governor's Daughter Promoted at Central Bank (The Cambodia Daily)

cases.category: bribery and abuse of authority charges
cases.people: Christodoulos Christodoulou (former governor); Andreas Vgenopoulos (Marfin Investment Group); Athina Christodoulou; Andreas Kizourides; Michalis Zolotas; Kyriacos Magiras and Michalis Fole (former Laiki Bank officials)
cases.summary: Former Central Bank of Cyprus governor Christodoulos Christodoulou and co-defendants faced 29 charges over a 1 million euro payment said to have been made so he would overlook Andreas Vgenopoulos's acquisition of a controlling stake in Laiki Bank, which failed in 2013. The first charge covers February to November 2006, when he was governor, and alleges he agreed to take 1 million euros from Vgenopoulos and Marfin Investment Group. He is also accused of failing to investigate whether MIG could control Laiki after it bought 9.98% of shares from Marfin Financial Group and 8.18% from the TOSCA fund on 6 February 2006 without central bank approval, and of two counts of abuse of authority; all defendants faced money laundering charges. Christodoulou said the money was an advance for ten years of consultancy; in October 2014 he pleaded guilty to tax evasion and was jailed for five months. The case was expected to go to the Nicosia criminal court at the end of September 2016; the report gives no verdict.
cases.source_title: Christodoulou faces 29 charges over Laiki payment (Cyprus Mail)

cases.people: A Mediaworks journalist in the RBNZ media lockup (unnamed); Michael Reddell (former RBNZ employee who runs a blog); Graeme Wheeler (governor)
cases.summary: Deloitte, engaged by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand on 11 March 2016 and reporting on 12 April 2016, found the source of the leak of the 10 March 2016 Official Cash Rate decision was a Mediaworks employee. A Mediaworks journalist in the media lockup emailed a draft story out of the lockup room without RBNZ approval shortly before 8am; another Mediaworks employee who overheard colleagues discussing the rate drop emailed Michael Reddell at 8.04am, ahead of the 9am announcement, and Reddell did not notify the RBNZ until 9.08am. Mediaworks self-reported on 5 April 2016. Deloitte judged the Minister of Finance's office unlikely to be the source.
cases.source_title: Report on the investigation into the OCR leak (Deloitte, for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand)

revolving_door.people: Mark W. Olson (Governor, Board of Governors, 2001-2006)
revolving_door.summary: Federal Reserve History states that Mark W. Olson joined First Bank System, now US Bancorp, and was named as an officer in 1969, and that in 1976 he was named president and chief executive officer of Security State Bank in Fergus Falls, Minnesota, a bank his father had been the lead organizer in chartering in 1957. The page states he was elected president of the American Bankers Association in 1986, and from 1988 to 1999 served as national director of Ernst & Young LLP's regulatory consulting practice for the financial services industry, before becoming staff director of the US Senate Banking Committee's Securities Subcommittee in 2000. He was sworn in as a member of the Board of Governors on December 7, 2001, and left on June 30, 2006. The page states he then became chairman of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, and in September 2009 joined Corporate Risk Advisors LLC as cochairman. He died in 2018. No ethics finding is recorded.
revolving_door.source_title: Mark W. Olson (Federal Reserve History)
revolving_door.move: First Bank System and Security State Bank into the Board of Governors

revolving_door.people: Joseph A. Erickson (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, 1948-1961)
revolving_door.summary: Federal Reserve History states that in 1920 Joseph A. Erickson began his long association with National Shawmut Bank in Boston, beginning as a clerk, being promoted to manager of the Credit Department in 1925 and to branch manager in 1926, becoming a vice president in 1928 and being elevated to executive vice president in 1942. The page states that in 1948 he was appointed president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, becoming its eighth president in December 1948 and serving until February 1961. He died in 1983. No ethics finding is recorded.
revolving_door.source_title: Joseph A. Erickson (Federal Reserve History)
revolving_door.move: National Shawmut Bank executive vice presidency to the Boston Fed presidency

revolving_door.people: Robert P. Forrestal (President, Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, 1983-1996)
revolving_door.summary: Federal Reserve History states that Robert P. Forrestal became president and chief executive officer of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta on December 7, 1983, and served until January 1, 1996. The page states that after retiring from the Bank he worked with the Atlanta law firm of Smith, Gambrell & Russell and served on several corporate boards, and that he was a member of the boards of directors of Equifax Inc., Genuine Parts Co., ING North America Co., and the ING Advisory Council in the Netherlands. He died in 2004. No ethics finding is recorded.
revolving_door.source_title: Robert P. Forrestal (Federal Reserve History)
revolving_door.move: Atlanta Fed presidency to the board of ING North America and the ING Advisory Council

revolving_door.people: Dato' Dr. Nirmala Menon (Independent Non-Executive Member of the Board of Directors, appointed 16 March 2020; chairs the Board Risk Committee)
revolving_door.summary: Bank Negara Malaysia's own board-of-directors page gives Nirmala Menon's career before and alongside her central bank seat. The page lists, among her past roles, President and Chief Executive Officer of ING Malaysia Berhad, Head of South Asia at ING Asia Pacific Limited, Executive Vice President at MetLife Asia Pacific Limited, and board member of AXA Affin General Insurance Berhad and Avicennia Capital Sdn Bhd. It also lists her current outside board seats, which include Singlife Holdings Private Limited, a Singapore insurer, and Sime Darby Berhad. She was appointed to the central bank's board on 16 March 2020 as an independent non-executive member and chairs its Board Risk Committee. ING, MetLife, AXA and Singlife are insurance and financial-services groups; the Bank Negara page does not use the words private or state-owned for any of them, and it gives no start or end dates for any of the roles, only the date of her board appointment. So the direction and the firms are stated by the central bank itself, but the page does not characterise the ownership of any employer, and the exact years she held the ING and MetLife jobs are not stated here. This is a different person from the two revolving-door records Malaysia already holds.
revolving_door.source_title: Board of Directors (Bank Negara Malaysia)
revolving_door.move: from chief executive of insurer ING Malaysia and executive roles at MetLife Asia Pacific into a Bank Negara Malaysia board seat
